Country explicit (Respublica Salvatoriana).

rubric_latin: BASILICAE MINORIS HONORIBUS PRIVILEGIISQUE DECORATUR ECCLESIA PAROECIALIS DEO IN HONOREM B. MARIAE VIRGINIS DICATA ET IN LOCO « ARCACHON » ARCHIDIOECESIS BURDIGALENSIS POSITA.
incipit_latin: Exstat in Gallia, intra Burdigalensis archidioecesis fines, urbs quaedam non ita frequens, vulgato nomine « Arcachon » appellata
notes: Basilica Minor elevation; attests 'Cum Deiparae ab « Arcachon » Effigies, per Litteras Apostolicas sub anulo Piscatoris Pii PP. IX, fel. rec., Decessoris Nostri, anno MDCCCLXX datas, aurea corona esset redimita'. 1870 is the year of the granting Litterae of Pius IX; the actual crowning ceremony date is not given. The image is a small alabaster statue of the BVM with the Infant Jesus found by the Franciscan Thomas Illyricus in the early 16th c. Vernacular form 'Notre-Dame d'Arcachon' rendered from the Latin 'Nostrae Dominae de Arcachon'. Act begins on printed page 714 (passage indexed at 715).

act_type: Litterae Apostolicae / Breve (Ex Secretaria Brevium; Ad perpetuam rei memoriam)
rubric_latin: Ecclesia B. M. V. Dominae Nostrae a Spe, Briconii extans, ad Basilicam minorem evehitur.
incipit_latin: Vetustis sacris aedibus Deo in honorem Deiparae Virginis dicatis, ac splendidiorem ipsius cultum in Gallia efferentibus, merito accensenda est
notes: Retrospective mention inside a minor-basilica elevation: "Pervetustum ipsius Virginis Dei Genitricis simulacrum, prodigiis clarum, aureoque diademate Summi Pontificis nomine anno 1865 redimitum" - i.e. crowned with a golden diadem in the name of the Supreme Pontiff in 1865. Country France is explicit ("in Gallia"); pilgrims come especially from Brittany ("e Britanniae praesertim regionibus"). Place given by OCR as "Briconii"; identified as Saint-Brieuc because the petitioner is "Petrus Maria Fallieres Episcopus Briocensis et Trecorensis" - hence confidence medium rather than high. Other OCR damage on that page: "condecoran" for "condecorari", "supplicia ... vota" for "supplicia"/"supplicia vota". The coronation sentence stands on printed p. 400, just above the assigned passage window (the passage, printed_page 402, contains the end of this act); page recorded as 400 where the act and the coronation notice begin. Act dated 20 December 1902 (pontificate year 25) though printed in vol. 36 (1903-04).

rubric_latin: AD R. P. D. FRANCISCUM M. GIEURE, BAIONENSIUM EPISCOPUM, OCCASIONE CORONATIONE B. MARIAE V. « DU BEAU RAMEAU », AD TEMPLUM BÉTHARRAM.
incipit_latin: Dies non longe abest, ut affertur, cum indicta per te sacra sollemnitas cultores Virginis du Beau Rameau ad Bétharram congregabit
notes: Source passage in this batch is the volume index (printed p. 751, 'Dies non longe. - Ad R. P. D. Franciscum M. Gieure ... occasione coronationis B. M. Virginis « du Beau Rameau », ad templum Bétharram'); the act itself was read in txt/AAS-04-1912-ocr.txt at printed p. 490, so `page` is set to 490 rather than the index page 751. The same volume's analytic index (batch passage AAS-04-1912-ocr#g771, p. 771) repeats it: 'Gieure Franciscus ... epistolam accipit, qua ei fit potestas B. M. V. « du Beau Rameau » ad Bétharram decorandi aureis coronis a beatissimo Patre oblatis, 490.' Key act wording: 'idemque binas afferet áureas coronas, quibus tibi divinae Matris Filiique effigiem, sollemnibus caeremoniis, exornandi facimus potestatem' — the Pope sends two golden crowns via Victor Bourdenne, Procurator General, and grants the diocesan bishop the faculty to crown the image of the Virgin and Child. OCR of the rubric reads 'GIBURE' for GIEURE and 'CORONATIONE' for CORONATIONIS. coronation_date: the letter (14 June 1912) says the solemnity is imminent ('Dies non longe abest'), and the index heads the letter 'occasione coronationis', so the year 1912 is stated in substance; no day/month given. Country inferred from the diocese of Bayonne, named in the rubric.

rubric_latin: LITTERAE APOSTOLICAE quibus LEO PP. XIII gratulatur Archiepiscopo Cameracen, de felici exitu Incoronationis B. Mariae Virginis « Des Dunes ».
incipit_latin: Praestans fidei ac pietatis exemplum urbe Dunkerque inter multas laetitiae demonstrationes Incoronationis Nostrae Dominae des Dunes causa excitatas
notes: Papal letter of congratulation to Etienne-Marie-Alphonse (Sonnois), Archbishop of Cambrai, on the coronation of Notre-Dame des Dunes at Dunkerque; it attests the coronation rather than granting it, hence retrospective_attestation. The act is printed in French on p. 10 ('le couronnement de Notre Dame des Dunes'), with the Latin 'Versio' on p. 11 — the incipit given here is from that Versio; the French incipit after the salutation is 'L'eclatant exemple de foi et de piete donne publiquement, ces jours derniers, par la ville de Dunkerque'. No word for image/simulacrum appears: the source names only the devotional title. Coronation date not stated beyond 'ces jours derniers' / 'diebus nuper transactis' before the Datum of 10 June 1903, so only the year is recorded. Datum line: 'Donne a Rome pres Saint-Pierre, le 10 Juin 1903, de Notre Pontificat la vingt sixieme annee'. No mention of the Vatican Chapter or of a Legate. Also indexed in the volume's Summa Actorum (p. 758) and Index (p. 764) as 'de felici exitu Incoronationis B. M. V. des Dunes ... 10'. OCR of the Latin version reads 'iurganti pietatis aemulationi' (probably 'certanti'/'urgenti') and 'excitati Auctus' for 'fluctus' — repairs not applied to quoted text.

rubric_latin: ECCLESIA PAROECIALIS DEO IN HONOREM « NOSTRAE DOMINAE » DICATA, IN CIVITATE « GRAY » ARCHIDIOECESIS BISUNTINAE POSITA, PRIVILEGIIS BASILICAE MINORIS HONESTATUR.
incipit_latin: Insigne pietatis, historiae artisque monumentum Ecclesiam paroecialem, Deo in honorem « Nostrae Dominae » civitatis vulgo « Gray » dicatam
notes: Basilica Minor act; coronation attested in passing: 'cujus prodigiosum Simulacrum cives ipsi atque peregrini summa pietate venerantur, praesertim ex quo auctoritate ac nomine fel. rec. Decessoris Nostri Pii Pp. X, anno MCMIX, corona aurea redimitum fuit' (OCR prints 'MCMTX' for MCMIX). Country explicit ('intra Bisuntinae Archidioeceseos fines in Gallia').

act_type: Decretum (S. Congregatio Indulgentiis Sacrisque Reliquiis praeposita)
legate: Archiepiscopus Bituricensis (Archbishop of Bourges; personal name not given in the text)
rubric_latin: Quo conceditur ut Archisodalitas Bmae V. Mariae a « S. Corde Iesu, » ab Ecclesia S. Andreae de Valle transferri possit in Ecclesia B. Mariae V. D. Nostrae in Foro Agonali.
incipit_latin: Ab anno 1854 Presbyterorum Societas Exsolduni in Archidioecesi Bituricensi in Galliis florere coepit, qui vires, consilia et operam ad vineam Domini sacris expeditionibus potissimum excolendam contulerunt
notes: Decree transferring the Archconfraternity of Our Lady of the Sacred Heart from S. Andrea della Valle to the church in the Piazza Navona; it recalls in passing that the Apostolic See 'nomine proprio coronam Simulacro imponendi facultatem largita est Archiepiscopo Bituricensi' — granted the Archbishop of Bourges the faculty of imposing the crown, in the Holy See's own name, on the Issoudun image. No date is given for the grant or for the coronation itself, so coronation_date is null. Datum: 'Romae, ex Secretaria Sacrae Congregationis Indulgentiis Sacrisque Reliquiis praepositae dic 26 Aprilis 1879' ('dic' = 'die'); the act is dated 1879 although the volume (ASS 11) is labelled 1878 — the volume runs over into 1879; trusted the act. OCR repairs in the incipit: 'Exsokluni' -> 'Exsolduni', 'in Gallus' -> 'in Galliis'. Elsewhere 'Archisodalkate' -> 'Archisodalitate'. A second image, 'imago Dominae Nostrae a Sacratissimo Corde Iesu' left for public veneration at S. Andrea della Valle in Rome, is mentioned but no coronation is asserted of it, so no record was emitted for it.

legate: Carolus A. de la Tour d'Auvergne, Archiepiscopus Bituricensis (crowned 'nomine decessoris Nostri f. r. Pii IX')
rubric_latin: AD R. P. D. MARTINUM HIERONYMUM IZARD, ARCHIEPISCOPUM BITURICENSEM, QUINQUAGESIMO REDEUNTE ANNO CUM IMAGINI DOMINAE NOSTRAE A S. CORDE IESU IN BASILICA EXOLDUNENSI AUREA CORONA IMPOSITA EST.
incipit_latin: Inter mariales aedes, quibus Gallia feliciter nobilitatur, merito sane praeclarum locum obtinet Exoldunensis Basilica
notes: Letter of Benedict XV to Abp Martin Jerome Izard of Bourges for the golden jubilee of the coronation. The passage does not state the coronation year explicitly: it says the fiftieth year is about to be completed ('annus propediem expleatur quinquagesimus') since the crowning done by Abp de la Tour d'Auvergne in the name of Pius IX, and the jubilee solemnities are set for 8 September (letter dated 15 Aug 1919), hence 1869 - inferred, verify. The 'legate' field records the prelate who performed the original crowning in the Pope's name, not a legate deputed by this act. Rubric OCR read 'BITURICENSEM' as 'BITÜRICENSEM'.

legate: Emmanuel Caelestinus S. R. E. Cardinalis Suhard, then Archbishop of Reims, later of Paris
rubric_latin: ECCLESIA DEO IN HONOREM B. MARIAE V. DICATA, IN OPPIDO « LA GUERCHE DE BRETAGNE » IN GALLIA POSITA, INTRA RHEDONENSIS ARCHIDIOECESIS FINES, TITULO BASILICAE MINORIS ORNATUR.
incipit_latin: Tanta in populo christiano fuit semper, inde a prioribus Ecclesiae saeculis, erga Deiparam Virginem pietas, ut haud raro quaedam urbs
notes: Basilica Minor act; the clause on printed p. 725 reads: « ... quae a desideratissimo S. R. E. Presbytero Cardinali Emmanuele Caelestino Suhard, tunc Rhemensi postea Parisiensi Archiepiscopo, anno MCMXXXVII sollemni est pompa redimita ». Note that 'corona' / 'diademate' is not expressed — 'redimita' is used absolutely — so that this is a coronation is a reading of the standard AAS formula and should be verified. The vernacular title is a normalisation of the Latin 'de la Guerche' given in the text. The candidate passage is keyed to printed p. 725; the act begins on p. 724, which is cited here.

rubric_latin: SANCTUARIUM B. M. V. DE BONO SUCCURSU PAROECIAE DE LABLACHÈRE, DIOECESIS VIVARIENSIS INTRA FINES, BASILICAE MINORIS TITULO HONORIBUSQUE AUGETUR.
incipit_latin: Dioecesis Vivariensis intra fines in paroecia de Lablachere conspicuum exstat sanctuarium sub titulo Beatae Mariae Virginis a Bono Succursu
notes: Basilica Minor act granted on the fiftieth anniversary of the coronation: 'quodque prodigiis gratiisque clarum aureo diademate anno MDCCCLXXX Apostolica auctoritate coronatum est'. Country inferred from the diocese of Viviers and the French place name.

act_type: Decretum super virtutibus heroicis (Sacra Congregatio pro Causis Sanctorum)
rubric_latin: LEODIEN. Beatificationis et Canonizationis Servae Dei Eugeniae Joubert, Congregationis Sororum a S. Familia Ss. Cordis Iesu. SUPER DUBIO
notes: Passing mention only: 'Die 11 Februarii a. 1876, anniversaria manifestationis B. M. V. Lapurdi et coronationis eiusdem simulacri auctoritate Pii PP. IX factae'. Attests that the Lourdes image was crowned by authority of Pius IX, but gives no coronation date (11 February is given as the anniversary date, which a checker should verify). Country/diocese inferred from 'Lapurdi'. Not a papal act; decree of the Congregation for the Causes of Saints, hence pope=null.

rubric_latin: ECCLESIA NOSTRAE DOMINAE A MIRACULIS IN CIVITATE MAURIAC, DIOECESIS SANCTI FLORI, EXSTANS, AD TITULUM ET DIGNITATEM BASILICAE MINORIS EVEHITUR.
incipit_latin: Constat apprime ecclesiam a Nostra Domina a miraculis, sitam in urbe Mauriac appellata, quae est ex praecipuis civitatibus dioecesis Sancti Fiori in Gallia
notes: Basilica Minor act stating 'Vetus beatae Mariae Virginis a miraculis simulacrum ... anno MDCCCLV a Pio Pp. IX, rec. mem. Decessore Nostro, aureo diademate redimitum'. Act begins on printed page 493 (passage printed_page is 492). Rubric OCR 'SANCTI PLORI' repaired to 'SANCTI FLORI'.

legate: Cardinalis Archiepiscopus Bisuntinus (Summi Pontificis Legatus; name not stated)
rubric_latin: SANCTUARIUM B. M. V. VULGO « DE MONTE SION » NUNCUPATUM, IN DIOECESI NANCEIENSI ET TULLENSI, BASILICIS MINORIBUS ACCENSETUR.
incipit_latin: Seiuntensi in monte, vulgo Sion nuncupato, Dioecesis Tullensis intra fines, iam saeculo decimo fere exeunte, parva admodum exstabat Deiparae Virginis in honorem Deo dicata sacra aedes
notes: Coronation attested twice: 'post sollemnem coronationem a rec. mem. Decessore Nostro Pio Pp. IX decretam, atque anno MDCCCLXXIII a Cardinali Archiepiscopo Bisuntino Summi Pontificis Legato peractam' and 'hoc anno, sexagesimo ab eadem simulacri Deiparae sollemni pontificia coronatione'. The Legate is identified only by see (Besançon). Vernacular title is the standard French form of the Latin 'de Monte Sion'; locality given by the act as 'Seiuntensi in monte, vulgo Sion' in Lorraine. Passage printed_page 329; act opens on p. 328.

rubric_latin: TEMPLUM NOSTRAE DOMINAE A TABULIS INTER FINES CIVITATIS AC DIOECESIS MONTIS PESSULANI HONORIBUS BASILICAE MINORIS INSIGNITUR.
incipit_latin: Montis Pessulani in civitate in honorem Nostrae Dominae a Tabulis exstat ecclesia quae vetustate, molis amplitudine atque artis operibus, quibus est exornata, excellit.
notes: Basilica Minor grant. Attestation: 'Huiusmodi vero Beatae Virginis simulacrum, gratiis miraculisque clarum ... nomine Decessoris Nostri Leonis Pp. XIII aurea corona decoratum est' (OCR reads 'decora-tur, est'). Crowned in the name of Leo XIII, so between 1878 and 1903; no date given. The image is an 11th-cent. black wooden statue of the Virgin with the Infant Jesus. Passage printed_page 40, but the act begins on p. 39 (rubric visible in the context before the p. 40 running head). Country confirmed by the text's reference to the 'Gallicae Revolutionis' eversores; vernacular title (Notre-Dame des Tables) is not in the text.

rubric_latin: TITULUS AC PRIVILEGIA BASILICAE MINORIS CONFERUNTUR ECCLESIAE PAROECIALI BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS DE GAUDIO (« NOTRE DAME DE JOIE »), IN PAGO « PONTIVY » DIOECESIS VENETENSIS.
incipit_latin: Gaudii nuntia in hac lacrimarum valle ob vitae suae mysteria Beatissima Virgo Maria ab Ecclesia ac toto populo christiano semper habita est
notes: « ante pervetustam Beatae Mariae Virginis de Gaudio Iconem, auctoritate Decessoris Nostri Pii PP. XII, fel. rec., anno MCMLI, aurea redimitam corona ». Crowned 1951 by the authority of Pius XII; minister not named. Brittany/France explicit (« in Britannia Minori », « Gallici pagi »).

legate: Franciscus M. Serrand, Episcopus Briocensis
rubric_latin: R. P. D. FRANCISCUS M. SERRAND EPISCOPUS BRIOCENSIS DEPUTATUR AD AUREA CORONA DONANDUM SIMULACRUM B. M. V. « DE LA DÉLIVRANCE » OPPIDI QUENTIN.
incipit_latin: Uti ad Nos attulisti, in loco « Quentin » in tuae dioecesis intra fines sito, insigne exstat sanctuarium mariale sub titulo Beatae Mariae Virginis de la Délivrance
notes: The Pope commits to the Bishop of Saint-Brieuc that he himself crown the image 'die per te statuendo, post sollemnia Missarum, per te ipsum, servatis servandis, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, sollemni ritu aurea corona redimias' — date left to the bishop, so no coronation date. The immediately preceding act (I, pp. 222-223, same date) raises the same church to a minor basilica. Country inferred from the diocese of Saint-Brieuc.

rubric_latin: CURIALE TEMPLUM RHEDONENSE, SUB TITULO SS.MI SALVATORIS ET B. M. V. DE MIRACULIS ET VIRTUTIBUS, BASILICAE MINORIS DIGNITATE IN PERPETUUM COHONESTATUR.
incipit_latin: Rhedonensi in Urbe Curialis Ecclesia titulo Ssmi Salvatoris et B. Mariae Virginis de Miraculis et Virtutibus, non modo amplitudine sed etiam omnigenae artis conspicuis operibus praestans
notes: IMPORTANT for the checker: this act is NOT inside the assigned passage text — it is the immediately preceding act (no. XI) on printed p. 63 of the same volume, found while verifying passage AAS-09-I-1917-ocr#65 (whose context begins mid-p. 64). Included because it is an unambiguous attestation: 'prodigiosum nempe Virginis Deiparae simulacrum, anno MDCCCCVIII Decessoris Nostri Pii PP. X rec. me. nomine atque auctoritate ... sollemni pompa redimitum est aurea praedivite corona.' Same date and Pope as the following act. Confidence set to medium only because the source_id does not literally cover it.

rubric_latin: TITULUS BASILICAE MINORIS PRO PAROCHIALI ECCLESIA RHEDONENSI S. ALBINO EP. ET CONF. AC B. M. V. DE BONIS NUNTIIS DICATA.
incipit_latin: Conspicua Dei templa, quae non minus antiquitate et artis splendore, quam potissimum decore, cultu et fidelium celebritate excellant
notes: Basilica Minor act attesting a past crowning: 'Quare anno MCMVIII amplissimo Sacrorum Antistite adstante, Cleri et populi permagno concursu, sacrae Deiparae Virginis Mariae de Bonis Nuntiis imagini aureum diadema, de mandato rec. me. Pii Papae X Decessoris Nostri, sollemniter fuit impositum.' The clause falls on printed p. 65 (the passage's printed_page); the act opens on printed p. 64, used as aas_page. Country explicit ('inter Marialia Galliae Sanctuaria', 'Gallicae pietatis'). Crowning prelate not named.

legate: S. R. E. Cardinalis de Bonnechose, Rothomagensium antistes
rubric_latin: ECCLESIA ROTHOMAGENSIS B. M. VIRGINIS A BONO SUCCURSU TITULO AC PRIVILEGIIS BASILICAE MINORIS DECORATUR.
incipit_latin: Illustriores inter sacras Aedes, quae tum praestantibus artis operibus Galliae regiones illustrant, tum Francorum religionis alacre studium miramque munificentiam late praedicant
notes: Basilica minor act reporting the earlier coronation: « nono kalendas iunias anno millesimo octingentesimo octogesimo ... Cardinalis de Bonnechose ... pretiosissimum et auro et gemmis coronam, Decessoris Nostri ... Leonis Pp. XIII nomine, eidem simulacro Virginis et Infantis Iesu ... sollemni ritu imposuit ». 'nono kalendas iunias' converted to 24 May 1880. The crown was imposed on both the Virgin and the Infant Jesus. Act opens on printed page 226; the coronation clause is on page 227, so aas_page is the act's START page. 'legate' here is the prelate who actually crowned the image in Leo XIII's name, recorded retrospectively, not a legate deputed by this act.

rubric_latin: AEDES CURIALIS B. M. V. DE FUNICULO, IN CIVITATE VALENCIENNES, AD TITULUM AC DIGNITATEM BASILICAE MINORIS EVEHITUR.
incipit_latin: Templa Dei vetustis inclyta memoriis et fidelium religione celebria de more Romanorum Pontificum Decessorum Nostrorum, singularibus titulis privilegiisque decorare, pro re ac tempore, satagimus.
notes: Act begins on printed p. 492 (passage page 491). States that Leo XIII by Apostolic Letters sealed 16 March 1896 decreed the statue be solemnly crowned in his own name and authority ('statuam memoratam Virginis a Funiculo, ipsius Romani Pontificis nomine et auctoritate, sollemni ritu coronandum decrevit'); the date of the crowning itself is not given, so coronation_date left null. OCR gives the vernacular title as 'du Saint Gordon' (= du Saint Cordon).

legate: Cardinalis Donnet, tunc archiepiscopus Burdigalensis
rubric_latin: TITULO AC PRIVILEGIIS BASILICAE MINORIS HONESTATUS SANCTUARIUM MARIALE B. M. V. CONSOLATRICE AFFLICTORUM DE VERDELAIS, IN ARCHIDIOECESI BURDIGALENSI.
incipit_latin: Exstat in civitate Verdelais, intra fines archidioecesis Burdigalensis, iam inde a saeculo XII erectum, templum sive sanctuarium Mariale
notes: Clause: « quae, de speciali mandato fel. rec. Nostri Praedecessoris Pii PP. IX, iuxta Litteras Apostolicas, Piscatoris annulo die IV mensis maii anno MDCCCLV obsignatas, aureo diademate redimita fuit a bo. me. Cardinali Donnet, tunc archiepiscopo Burdigalensi, die II mensis iulii sequentis anni MDCCCLVI ». Papal mandate 4 May 1855; crowning 2 July 1856. 'legate' field records the prelate who crowned it by Pius IX's mandate (recorded retrospectively, not deputed by this act).

rubric_latin: BASILICAE MINORIS HONORIBUS DECORATUR ECCLESIA CATHEDRALIS VIRDUNENSIS, IN GALLIA.
incipit_latin: Mirabile itidemque haud commune privilegium vetustae Virodunensi Ecclesiae Cathedrali, in Gallia, eminentissimus Deus largitus est
notes: Basilica Minor act for Verdun cathedral; the coronation clause falls on printed p. 491, but the act opens on p. 490, so aas_page is the act's start page. Coronation clause: 'Marianum praesertim Simulacrum, quod ibidem magna devotione colitur, per Venerabilem Fratrem Angelum Iosephum Roncalli, Mesembrianum titularem Archiepiscopum, Apostolicum in Gallia Nostrum Nuntium, postridie Kalendas Iunias superiore anno, corona auro gemmisque distincta redimitum fuit.' Crowned not by a deputed Legate but by the Apostolic Nuncio to France, Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli (later John XXIII), hence 'legate' left null. coronation_date derived: 'postridie Kalendas Iunias' = 2 June; 'superiore anno' relative to the act's Datum (8 Sept 1947) = 1946 — verify. OCR of the rubric reads 'VIRDU-NENSIS' (line-break); correct form is presumably VIRODUNENSIS. Vernacular title is a rendering of the Latin 'Dominae Nostrae de Prodigiis seu de Viroduno'; not given in the text.

act_type: Causa apud S. Congregationem Rituum (concessio et approbatio Officii et Missae propriae) - Advocati defensio
rubric_latin: VENETEN. Concessionis et approbationis Officii et Missae propriae Manifestationis S. Imaginis B. Annae apud Britones pro die 7 martii, Officii et Missae propriae in honorem eiusdem S. Annae pro die 26 iulii, nec non concessionis et approbationis Missae votivae propriae.
incipit_latin: Intra fines cuiusdam paroeciae Pluneret nuncupatae, Dioecesis Venetensis, extat oppidum quoddam a S. Anna nomen habens
notes: Retrospective mention on printed p. 381: 'instanti Episcopo Venetensi sub die 22 maii 1868 Breve edidit quo nimirum tum Virginis Mariae, tum Annae simulacro corona imponi liceret.' The granting Brief of Pius IX is dated 22 May 1868; that is not the date of the document being reported, so act_date is null. The text does not say when (or whether) the crowning was actually carried out, so coronation_date is null. This record covers the image of the Virgin Mary; a companion record covers the image of St Anne. The passage does not state explicitly that the Marian image stands in the same sanctuary of St Anne - inferred from context, hence medium confidence. Page set to 373, where the item 'VENETEN. ...' begins (statement on p. 381); locality/diocese details taken from p. 373 of the same volume. Country: Brittany ('apud Britones', 'Britannia Armorica ... pars Galliae').

rubric_latin: AD R. P. D. ALCIMUM GOURAUD, EPISCOPUM VENETENSEM: TERTIO PLENO SAECULO AB APPARITIONE SANCTAE ANNAE, PROPE AURAY.
incipit_latin: Tertium affers completum iri proximo mense saeculum, ex quo, haud procul ab urbe vulgo Auray nuncupata, quae intra dioecesis istius tuae fines sita est, Sancta Anna
notes: 'praeterquam quod Pius IX et statuam corona aurea redimiri suo nomine iussit'. No year of the crowning is given. Rubric taken from p. 284 of the volume text (OCR 'ALCTMTJM GOURAUD ... AURAT'); the addressee is the Bishop of Vannes (Venetensis).

legate: Cardinalis Archiepiscopus Coloniensis (not named in the act)
rubric_latin: TITULUS BASILICAE MINORIS CONFERTUR PAROECIALI ECCLESIAE BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS CONSOLATRICIS AFFLICTORUM, OPPIDI KEVELAER, DIOECESIS MONASTERIENSIS.
incipit_latin: In civitate Kevelaer appellata, prope Regni Hollandici fines, intra limites Monasteriensis dioecesis posita, Mariale sanctuarium praeclarissimum exstat
notes: 'Iconem autem Virginis Decessor Noster rec. mem. Leo PP. XIII per Cardinalem Archiepiscopum Coloniensem anno MDCCCXC aureo diademate sollemni pompa ornatam voluit.' The crowning Cardinal Archbishop of Cologne is not named. Rubric OCR reads 'CONSOLATRICE?' for 'CONSOLATRICIS'. Country inferred from diocese of Münster/Kevelaer (act says it lies near the Dutch border, within the diocese of Münster).

rubric_latin: ECCLESIA IN HONOREM B. MARIAE V. A VISITATIONE, IN OPPIDO WERLA INTRA FINES PADERBORNENSIS ARCHIDIOECESIS CONSECRATA, BASILICIS MINORIBUS ACCENSETUR.
incipit_latin: Quam omnes gentes ex eiusmet vaticinio ferunt laudibus, Virgini Mariae hospitae consecratum Templum, Werlae intra fines archidioecesis Paderbornensis situm
notes: Basilica Minor elevation; attests 'Iuvat quoque memorare egregium hoc Simulacrum anno MDCCCCXI, magna adstante populi multitudine, aureo diademate esse redimitum'. The 13th-c. carved image was formerly venerated at Soest ('Susatium', Aedes « Sanctae Mariae ad pratum ») and translated to Werl in 1661. Country Germany explicit from the mention of Konrad Adenauer, head of the West German government. Act begins on printed page 479 (verified against page markers).

legate: Marius S. R. E. Cardinalis Casariego, archiepiscopus Guatimalensis
rubric_latin: Effigies B. M. Virginis a Rosario, quae in cathedrali templo Altensi servatur, pretioso diademate redimitur.
incipit_latin: Quo in honore Beatissima Virgo Maria sit per horum annorum decursum inter communitatem Altensem habita semper quantaque veneratione pariter exculta
notes: Act begins on printed p. 1212 (running head in context); passage indexed at p. 1211. The crowning is entrusted not to the local Ordinary (Bp 'Ansgarius García Urízar', Praesul Altensis — first name as OCR'd) but to Card. Mario Casariego, Archbishop of Guatemala, acting in the Pope's name. Diocese/country not named in the act: identified as Dioecesis Altensis = Los Altos, Quetzaltenango–Totonicapán, Guatemala, from other AAS acts (AAS 20 [1928] and AAS 43 [1951] erecting and delimiting it). Locality not stated (cathedral of the diocese).

rubric_latin: Titulo ac privilegiis Basilicae Minoris templum S. Dominici in civitate Guatimalensi decoratur.
incipit_latin: Rosarii preces, veluti mystica serta in honorem Christi Matris contexta eidemque Deiparae acceptissima, ad caelestia impetranda dona efficacissimae semper fuerunt.
notes: Basilica Minor act; coronation attested in passing: 'Postquam autem anno millesimo nongentesimo trigesimo quarto, praeclara imago, pretioso diademate redimita est et Beata Virgo Regina ac Patrona totius Guatimalensis dicionis declarata ...'. OCR prints 'Bosarii'/'Eosarii' for 'Rosarii' and 'Eegina' for 'Regina' (repaired here). Country explicit ('natio Guatimalensis').

legate: Valerianus Gracias, S. R. E. Cardinalis, Archiepiscopus Bombayensis
rubric_latin: TEMPLUM B. MARIAE V. DE MONTE, IN SUBURBIO BOMBAYENSIS URBIS EXSTANS, BASILICIS MINORIBUS ACCENSETUR, AC INSUPER BOMBAYENSI EMO ORDINARIO FACULTAS COMMITTITUR CORONANDI IMAGINEM B. MARIAE V. IN EODEM ASSERVATAM.
incipit_latin: Perfugium salutis et quasi propugnaculum Fidei perhibetur esse Templum Deiparae sacrum et in amoeno colle positum, unde Bombayam urbem et maris vastissimum aequor prospicias
notes: Reached from the back-of-volume analytic index entry « Coronatio. Imaginis B. M. V. de Monte, in suburbio Bombayensi, 252 » (index page 897); the act itself was retrieved and is cited at its own printed page 252. Grant: « ... aureo diademate, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, redimiri sineremus », with execution committed to the Archbishop of Bombay: « Bombayensi Ordinario ... eas partes committimus ut die per se ipso deligendo, Imagini Beatae Mariae Virginis de Monte ... auream coronam, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, imponat ». The Archbishop is deputed as executor, not formally styled Legatus; date of crowning left to him.

rubric_latin: SANCTUARIUM A MATRE DOMINI, INTRA FINES ARCHIDIOECESIS SALERNITANAE, TITULO BASILICAE MINORIS AUGETUR.
incipit_latin: Iam inde a saeculo post Christum natum XII, intra fines archidioecesis Salernitanae, vetus exstat sanctuarium titulo a Matre Domini
notes: Coronation clause: « Miraculis quidem inclyta Virginis imago, Apostolica auctoritate et sollemni ritu, anno MDCCLIX, diademate aureo redimita fuit ». Locality not named in the act, only 'intra fines archidioecesis Salernitanae'; supporting petitions come from the bishops of Salerno, Nocera, Cava and Sarno and from 'municipii Iuceriae Superioris' (OCR; most likely 'Nuceriae Superioris' = Nocera Superiore), which would place the shrine at Materdomini in Nocera Superiore — NOT asserted here, needs a checker. Act date OCR reads 'die xr mensis iunii, anno MDCCCCXXIII'; read as XI = 11 June 1923, verify.

rubric_latin: Beata Maria Virgo a gratiis constituitur Patrona principalis dioecesis Thelesinae seu Cerretanae, una cum Sancto Antonio de Padua, Confessore et Ecclesiae Doctore.
incipit_latin: « Quaeramus gratiam, et per Mariam quaeramus », ait Sanctus Bernardus, suavissimus vitae spiritualis praeceptor ac Deiparae Virginis praeco eximius
notes: Patronage act attesting the crowning: 'Quod simulacrum, anno MDCCCXCIII aureo diademate sollemni ritu redimitum' (1893); no crowning authority named. The sanctuary is located only as 'urbis episcopalis praeclarum ornamentum' — i.e. in the episcopal city of the see of Telese/Cerreto Sannita — so locality left null rather than inferred. Vernacular title supplied from the Latin 'a gratiis'. Country inferred, not stated.

rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA V. « A REMEDIO » TOTIUS ARCHIDIOECESIS ARBORENSIS PATRONA AEQUE PRINCIPALIS CUM S. ARCHELAO MARTYRE INSTITUITUR.
incipit_latin: Ex quo Beatissima Virgo Maria, a remedio vulgo appellata et Arboreae pie exculta, aurea fuit corona redimita, pietas erga eandem hanc Dei hominumque Matrem
notes: Patronage act opens by recalling « aurea fuit corona redimita »; no year and no crowning authority stated. Sardinia is named in the act (« non solum e Sardinia insula sed e continente etiam terra »), so the country is secure; the exact locality of the sanctuary is not given.

rubric_latin: TEMPLUM SANCTI FRANCISCI ASSISIENSIS SEU SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE VIRG. IMMACULATAE, IN CIVITATE AGRIGENTINA EXSTANS, BASILICIS MINORIBUS ACCENSETUR.
incipit_latin: Refert ad Nos Venerabilis Frater Agrigentinus Episcopus intra fines civitatis suae episcopalis conspicuum titulo Sancti Francisci Assisiensis templum exstare
notes: Basilica Minor act; coronation attested in passing: 'anno proxime elapso Marianum ipsum simulacrum, Decreto Capituli Sacrosanctae Basilicae Vaticanae aurea corona est honestatum'. Coronation year 1940 derived from 'anno proxime elapso' relative to the act's year (MCMXXXXI); the year itself is not printed. Act day OCR-damaged: 'die rr m. Iulii, an. MCMXXXXI' (probably 'die II'), so act_date left null. Venerated image is a wooden statue ('veneranda lignea statua').

rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA VIRGO, « MADONNA DEL PONTELUNGO » NUNCUPATA, CIVITATIS AC DIOECESIS ALBINGANENSIS PATRONA CAELESTIS DECLARATUR EIUSDEMQUE FESTUM CERTA DIE STATUITUR.
incipit_latin: Qua Augustus Imperator Arociae fluvio in finibus Ingaunorum sublimen et artificiosum iniecerat pontem, ut viatorum commoditati consuleret
notes: Patron-declaration act. The only crowning statement is 'Hoc quippe Simulacrum, septies usque adhuc, maxima supplicum turba stipante, corona redimitum, coli atque observari numquam desiit' — the image has been crowned seven times so far; NO papal authority, date or agent is named, so this may not be a canonical papal coronation. Flagged for human check. The image is a 1502 triptych panel painting of the Virgin with the Divine Infant holding the keys of Albenga. Passage printed_page was 592; act begins on printed p. 591.

rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA VIRGO A « VALLEVIRIDE » CIVITATIS AC DIOECESIS ALGHERIENSIS PATRONA CAELESTIS AEQUE PRINCIPALIS DECLARATUR.
incipit_latin: Augustissimam coeli Reginam, gratiarum omnium apud Deum sequestram, miserentissimam exsulum Hevae filiorum consolatricem, in universo catholico orbe, hac lacrimabili maiorum tempestate
notes: Patron-declaration act; coronation attested in passing on printed p. 175: « Quem Sanctissimae Deiparae triumphum conclusit sollemnis memoratae Imaginis coronatio, ex concessione Capituli Patriarchalis Basilicae Vaticanae, in Templo Cathedrali Algheriensi peracta ». Crowned by concession of the Vatican Chapter, not by a papal act. The year is not stated; the surrounding narrative places it in 'superiore anno' relative to the Datum of 25 March 1949, hence 1948 — verify. The candidate passage is keyed to printed p. 175; the act begins on p. 174, which is cited here. OCR rubric reads 'VALLEYTRIDE' (repaired to VALLEVIRIDE).

rubric_latin: ANCONITAN. ET HUMAN. EVECTIONIS AD DIGNITATEM ARCHIEPISCOPALEM HONORIS CAUSA. Sedes Episcopalis Anconitana evehitur in Archiepiscopalem honoris causa.
incipit_latin: Honoribus et privilegiis cumulare civitates tum incolarum frequentia tum nobilitate conspicuas, eas praesertim quae ab aetate Apostolica christianam fidem amplexatae sunt
notes: Retrospective mention of a personal papal coronation, on printed p. 198: 'quamque gloriosus Pontifex Pius VII, Savona ubi captivus fuerat rediens, suis manibus aurea corona donavit.' Crowned by Pius VII with his own hands on his return from captivity at Savona; no date is given in the text (Pius VII's return journey was in 1814), so coronation_date is null. Page set to 195, where the decree begins ('EX S. CONGREGATIONE CONSISTORIALI - ANCONITAN. ET HUMAN.'); the coronation statement is on p. 198 and the Datum (14 September 1904) on p. 200 - rubric, incipit and date taken from the full volume text. Country derived from Ancona/Picenum/Adriatic. OCR running head reads 'Ancoriitan.'.

rubric_latin: TITULUS ET PRIVILEGIA BASILICAE MINORIS CONFERUNTUR METROPOLITANAE ECCLESIAE S. CYRIACI EP. M. ANCONAE, SACRIS RELIQUIIS ET PRODIGIIS PRAECLARAE.
incipit_latin: Metropolitanum Anconae templum in excelso civitatis colle situm, late mare prospiciens Hadriacum, saeculo octavo exeunte traditur fuisse erectum
notes: The passage itself is the volume's Index rerum analyticus (printed p. 491), whose entry reads 'Pius PP. VII, 201; redimivit corona imaginem Reginae omnium Sanctorum, Anconae, 14'. Verified against the act in the same volume file: the Litterae Apostolicae raising the metropolitan church of Ancona to a minor basilica begin on printed p. 13 and state on p. 14 'Imaginem thaumaturgam titulo Reginae Sanctorum omnium excultam, a captivitate redux sa. me. Pius PP. VII Praedecessor Noster, maxima populi ac civitatis laetitia, aurea gemmataque corona sollemni pompa redimivit'. So the crowning was performed personally by Pius VII after his return from captivity (i.e. after 1814; no date given - coronation_date null); it is here reported retrospectively inside a basilica-minor act of Pius XI, hence retrospective_attestation rather than papal_personal_coronation. The image is a Marian image painted on linen on one of the principal altars. Datum line: 'die xiv mensis Iulii anno MDCCCCXXVI'. page set to 13 (act begins) though the coronation sentence and the index citation are on p. 14. Country 'Italy' inferred from Ancona / 'inter sacras Piceni aedes'; confidence dropped to medium for that reason only - the coronation fact itself is explicit.

legate: Raphael S. R. E. Cardinalis Merry del Val, Archipresbyter Capituli Vaticani
rubric_latin: ECCLESIA ORDINIS CARMELITARUM, ARENZANI IN ARCHIDIOECESI IANUENSI, PUERO IESU PRAGENSI SACRA, BASILICAE MINORIS HONORIBUS CONDECORATUR.
incipit_latin: Pragensem Pueri Iesu Imaginem christifideles omnes non modo quidem in Pragensi ecclesia a Carmelitis nuncupata, sed etiam multis aliis in locis, ubique terrarum, colunt et celebrant
notes: Coronation attested: 'quam anno MDCCCCXXIV die XXIV Februarii, aureo gemmatoque diademate per decretum Patriarchalis Sacrosanctae Basilicae Vaticanae Capituli, dilectus filius Noster Raphael ... Cardinalis Merry del Val ... sollemni ritu ... coronavit'. Crowning done by the Archpriest of the Vatican Chapter (not strictly a papal legate); classified as retrospective attestation within the basilica minor act. Passage printed_page 321; act opens on p. 320.

rubric_latin: Beata Maria Virgo a Gratiis, vulgo « Madonna delle Grazie » nuncupata, una cum S. Aemygdio, urbis ac dioecesis Asculanae in Piceno praecipua Patrona renuntiatur.
incipit_latin: Ex quo, anno scilicet proxime praeterito, praeclara Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis a Gratiis, quae in sacrario apud Basilicam cathedralem Asculanam in Piceno asservatur
notes: Patron declaration opening 'Ex quo, anno scilicet proxime praeterito, praeclara Imago ... auctoritate Petriani Canonicorum Collegii, aureo diademate fuit redimita'. Coronation year 1960 derived from 'anno proxime praeterito' relative to the act date. The Datum line is OCR'd 'die XXVIII mensis Aprilis, anno m c m x x i' — MCMXXI is an OCR corruption of MCMLXI (1961), confirmed by 'Pontificatus Nostri tertio' and the volume year. Country Italy inferred from Asculum in Piceno; not stated.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, f. 296r
rubric_latin: corone d'oro fatte per le Sacre Imagini della Beatissima Vergine, e suo Santo Bambino detta della Santa Cintura nella Chiesa di S. Bartolo delli PP. Teatini nella Città di Assisi
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'corone d'oro fatte per le Sacre Imagini della Beatissima Vergine, e suo Santo Bambino'. Only a single payment mandate (8 March 1727, 80 scudi on account to the silversmith Giacomo Antonio Giardini, signed by Gio. Andrea Ricci, canon deputy) filed inside the Naples Purità dossier; no supplica, decree, instrument or relazione for this image appears in the range. 'S. Bartolo' as read; the crowns were already made by 1727.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 2r–23v.[02.mn.0000]
act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, relazione, stampa
legate: Giovanni Battista Missiroli, Bishop of Bertinoro ('Jo. Baptista ... Epus Brittinorij', 'Monsignor Missiroli, Vescovo di Bertinoro')
deputy: Giovanni Battista Missiroli, Bishop of Bertinoro ('Jo. Baptista ... Epus Brittinorij', 'Monsignor Missiroli, Vescovo di Bertinoro')
register_refs: ['Caps. 29. f. 379', 'Caps: 39. fasc: 309', "Raffaelli Sinodo Lib. II. MS. nell' Arch. Vat.no Capitolare pag. 45. §. XXXI"]
rubric_latin: Dell' Immagine di Maria detta la Madonna del Lago, che si venera nella Chiesa situata fuori di Bertinoro
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'duas Coronas aureas ponderis Scutor. Quadraginta unius cum dimidio auri'. Petitioner: Abbate Francesco Giacinto Ascensini, Provost of the cathedral of Bertinoro (original instances to the Chapter); execution then solicited by Bishop Missiroli in May 1705 and by Abbot Vitale Ascevolini of S. Maria d'Urano. Place-name OCR forms: 'Brecinoca' (f.2r silversmith account), 'Brictinorii', 'Brittinorij', 'Britonorij', 'Ber-gamoro'; abbey 'de Urano' also OCR'd as 'de Trano', 'de Prano'. Concession date 1689-06-20 comes from the margin note '20. Junii 1689 conced.' on the near-empty title leaf f.5v ('Conc[essione] dell'Ill'mo e R'mo Capitolo di S. Pietro delle Corone d'oro', signed 'Gio: Giardini Agt.o'); the crowns' inscription and the 1789 engraving say the crown was donated 'Anno 1704', and the Chapter's delegation letter is dated Rome 13 June 1705. Coronation on the theatre in the piazza of Bertinoro on 9 Aug 1705 (instrument 'die nona mensis Augusti' 1705; printed relazione: feasts 8-11 Aug 1705, crowning on Sunday). Documents in order: f.2r silversmith's account (two crowns, 41.5 scudi); f.3r-4r extract from Raffaelli's MS synod with instrument summary ('other'); f.5v concession title leaf ('decretum'); f.6r-16r printed 'Vera, e distinta relazione' (Cesena, Demetrio Degni, 1705) with an inserted 1789 engraving by Cavallucci/Bombelli; f.17r inserted printed odes for the 1805 centenary (one copy OCR'd as '1826'/'1851', likely misread); f.19r-22r notarial instrument of donation and receipt by Petrus Dominicus Toninus, incorporating the Chapter's letter of 13 June 1705 and the monks' mandate of 8 Aug 1705; f.22v bishop's attestation of the notary, 27 Aug 1705, with archivist margin note 'Inś Declarationis ... Die 9. Augś 1705' and 'Caps: 39. fasc: 309'; f.23r-v bishop's letter of thanks to the Chapter, Bertinoro 27 Aug 1705, in two copies (second copy dateline OCR'd 'Ostiglia', signature 'Cristoforo Vin.co Di Berrini' garbled). The two register refs 'Caps. 29. f. 379' and 'Caps: 39. fasc: 309' probably refer to the same instrument with an OCR discrepancy.

rubric_latin: Beata Maria Virgo « a Quercu » principalis caelestis Patrona declaratur convallis « Nure » vulgo appellatae, intra fines Placentinae dioecesis.
incipit_latin: Amicum sidus in huius saeculi fluctibus exasperato mari omnibus lucet, augusta videlicet Maria: hanc si mortales intuentur, a recto cursu nequaquam aberrant
notes: Patron declaration stating 'Petrianum vero Canonicorum Collegium die XX mensis Februarii anno MCMXX indulsit, ut eiusdem Caelestis Virginis imago ibidem asservata aureo diademate sollemni ritu redimiretur'. 1920-02-20 is the date of the Vatican Chapter's indult, not necessarily of the ceremony, so only the year is recorded here. Country Italy inferred from the diocese of Piacenza / Val Nure; not stated. Vernacular title supplied as the usual rendering of 'a Quercu'.

rubric_latin: BASILICAE MINORIS HONORIBUS DECORATUR TEMPLUM IN HONOREM S. MARTINI EP. DEO DICATUM SEU SANCTUARIUM DEIPARAE A MONTE CARMELO, IN URBE BONONIENSI ORDINI FRATRUM CARMELITARUM CONCREDITUM.
incipit_latin: Bononiensi in urbe templum in honorem Sancti Martini Episcopi Deo dicatum exstat, curis ministerioque concreditum Ordinis Fratrum Carmelitarum
notes: Passage printed_page was 33; the act begins on printed p. 32, used here. Text: 'quodque aureo diademate, Capituli Vaticani decreto iam anno millesimo septingentesimo quarto exornatum, ab hodierno Archiepiscopo ... Ioanne Baptista S.R.E. Cardinali Nasalli Rocca di Corneliano iterum anno millesimo nongentesimo trigesimo nono decoratum est' — i.e. first crowned 1704 by decree of the Vatican Chapter, re-crowned 1939 by Card. Nasalli Rocca.

rubric_latin: Eminentissimo Archiepiscopo Bononiensi Breve, quo indulgentiae quaedam a Sanctissimo conceduntur.
incipit_latin: Qui vel a teneris annis singulari obsequio, intimoque cordis affectu sanctam Dei Genitricem Mariam coluimus
notes: Pius IX grants the Cardinal Archbishop of Bologna, 'tamquam Delegatum Nostrum', the faculty to place a golden crown 'Nostro nomine' on the image on 15 August of the current year ('hoc vertente anno, die decimaquinta mensis Augusti'); since the Brief is dated 16 July 1875, the coronation date is 1875-08-15. Classified papal_coronation_act because this document IS the granting act (it also has the character of a delegation). The delegate is addressed only as 'Venerabilis Frater' / 'Eminentissimo Archiepiscopo Bononiensi' and is not named, hence legate: null. Petitioner: Archangelus Maria Gatti, Abbot Visitator General of the Canons Regular of the Lateran. Act begins on printed p. 167 under the heading 'EX VATICANO' (passage printed_page was 168). OCR: 'supradicto cognationis die' read as 'coronationis die'; 'translatant' for 'translatam'. Volume 9 = 1876 but the Brief is of 1875. Country derived from 'Bononiae'.

rubric_latin: Basilicae Minoris honoribus decoratur ecclesia Beatae Mariae Virginis a Gratiis Brixiae consecrata.
incipit_latin: Meritis celebratur praeconiis Brixianum templum Beatae Mariae Virginis a Gratiis, quod antiquitate, mole, structurae genere artificiosisque operibus est admodum insigne
notes: Basilica Minor elevation stating 'Hoc Simulacrum, aureo diademate anno MDCCCLXXXVI auctoritate Petriani Canonicorum Collegii redimitum'. Country Italy inferred from Brixia/Brescia and 'Insubris regionis'; not stated. Vernacular title supplied as the usual rendering of 'a Gratiis'.

rubric_latin: Titulus ac privilegia Basilicae Minoris ecclesiae cathedrali Caesenatensi conferuntur.
incipit_latin: Merito praedicatur templum princeps Caesenas, quod saeculo xiv Romanico, uti appellant, architectandi genere exstructum, amplitudine molis commendatur et cultu multiplici.
notes: Basilica Minor elevation stating that Pius VI, on his return from Vienna, personally crowned the image: 'quorum priorem, Vindobona reducem, imaginem Beatae Mariae Virginis, eodem in templo excultam, aureo diademate redimivisse'. No year given (Pius VI's return from Vienna was 1782, not stated in the text). This is therefore a retrospective attestation of a personal papal coronation. Country Italy inferred from Caesena/Cesena; not stated.

act_type: Causa apud S. Congregationem Rituum (concessio et approbatio Officii et Missae propriae) cum informatione praevia
rubric_latin: INSULAE SARDINIAE. CONCESSIONIS ET APPROBATIONIS OFFICII ET MISSAE PROPRIAE IN HONOREM B. V. A BONO AERE NUNCUPATAE.
incipit_latin: Antequam referam S. Congregationis Decretum, nonnulla indicabo, quae ostendunt, quomodo solent eiusmodi causae pertractari
notes: Key sentence, on printed p. 354: 'Insignis haec B. Virginis imago ex Capituli Vaticani Decreto die 24 Aprilis 1870 aurea corona rite decorata est.' Crowning by the Chapter of St Peter's (Capitulum Vaticanum). Page set to 353, where the item ('INSULAE SARDINIAE ...') begins; the coronation statement is on p. 354. The passage is the editorial 'Brevis informatio' preceding the S.R.C. decree, hence incipit_latin is the editorial opening, not an act body. Vernacular title taken from the Italian book cited in the text ('Della statua miracolosa di Maria Vergine di Bonaria'). Volume 6 spans 1870-71; the related decree is dated 22 April 1871. Country derived from 'in Sardiniae insula' / 'Calarim'. OCR of the rubric reads 'A BONO AÈRE'.

legate: Caietanus Card. Bisleti
rubric_latin: AD EM.UM P. D. CAIETANUM PROTODIACONUM S. AGATHAE S. R. E. CARDINALEM BISLETI: QUEM LEGATUM MITTIT CALARIM AD MARIALIA SOLLEMNIA.
incipit_latin: Insignis admodum ac perantiqua est Marialis aedes quae, in Calaritana urbe sita, a Bono Aere nuncupatur
notes: Re-coronation after the sacrilegious theft of the crowns of the Virgin and the Child three years earlier (c. 1923): 'te ... his Litteris eligimus qui coronam auream simulacro Virginis de Bono Aere nomine et auctoritate Nostra imponas'. The act also attests the earlier crowning by the Vatican Chapter ('a Vaticano Capitulo corona aurea redimita sit', dated 1870 by AAS 18 [1926] 376). Coronation year 1926 inferred: the solemnities were being prepared at the date of the letter (25 March 1926) and the new church was inaugurated 22 April 1926 per AAS 18 (1926) 376.

rubric_latin: SANCTUARIUM B. M. V. DE BONARIA CALARITANAE CIVITATIS IN BASILICAM MINOREM EVEHITUR.
incipit_latin: Calaritana in civitate ac dioecesi sanctuarium Beatae Mariae Virginis de Bonaria nuncupatae exstat, curis religiosorum sodalium ex Ordine Beatae Mariae Virginis de Mercede concreditum
notes: 'in quo antiqua et prodigiosa Virginis effigies, iam aureo diademate anno MDCCCLXX per decretum Capituli Vaticani redimita, colitur'. Same image as AAS 18 (1926) 302. The act also notes the inauguration of the new church on 22 April 1926 and the 1908 proclamation of the Virgin of Bonaria as principal patron of Sardinia by Pius X.

rubric_latin: Titulo ac privilegiis Basilicae Minoris honestatur ecclesia Beatae Mariae Virgini in Caelum Assumptae sacra, vulgo « Madonna del Monte » seu « Conadomini » appellata et in urbe Calatayeronio posita.
incipit_latin: Praesidium decusque urbis Calatayeronii esse perhibetur templum Beatae Mariae Virginis in Caelum Assumptae sacrum, quod a Monte, cui est impositum, vulgo solet vocari
notes: Basilica Minor act. Coronation mentioned only as an anniversary: 'Revoluto vero quinquagesimo anno ex quo simulacrum Almae Deiparae, cui nomen « Conadomini », aureo diademate fuit redimitum' — the 50th year since the crowning, which with an act of 1963 implies c. 1913, but no year is stated, so coronation_date left null. No crowning authority named. Diocese spelled 'Calatayeronensis' in the OCR (for Calatagironensis/Caltagirone); bishop named 'Franciscus Fasola'. Act begins on printed p. 911; the coronation sentence is on p. 912 (the passage's printed_page). Country inferred, not stated.

rubric_latin: Sanctuarium Civitatis Castelli dioecesis, quod in loco « Colle di Canoscio » est dicatum beatae Mariae Virgini titulo « Madonna del Transito » invocatae, ad Basilicae minoris gradum dignitatemque evehitur.
incipit_latin: Inter sacras aedes Civitatis Castelli dioecesis merito celebratur sanctuarium beatae Mariae Virginis titulo « Madonna del Transito » invocatae, quod exstat in loco « Colle di Canoscio »...
notes: Basilica Minor elevation which attests that the painted image was solemnly crowned in 1888 by Card. Serafino Vannutelli in the name of the Vatican Chapter ('ab Eminentissimo Cardinale Seraphino Vannutelli, nomine Petriani Canonicorum Collegii, anno MDCCCLXXXVIII sollemni ritu coronatam'). Country not stated; inferred from Città di Castello.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 242r–245v
act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, instrumentum donationis, other
legate: the diocesan bishop, who imposed the crown in pontificals (name OCR-garbled: 'Ill.mus D. Card.lis Octavianus Acciaioli ... Ep.o Vercellensis')
deputy: the diocesan bishop, who imposed the crown in pontificals (name OCR-garbled: 'Ill.mus D. Card.lis Octavianus Acciaioli ... Ep.o Vercellensis')
rubric_latin: in Ecclesia Parochiali B. M. Virginis Mariæ Fontis Miraculorum Caravaggii Cremonen. diœcesis
notes: Crowns: one ('una Corona d'Oro Grande Tonda all'imperiale ... per la Ill.ma Madonna di Caravaggio'). Conto (242r): one crown weighing 128 scudi 2 den. 12 gr. of gold, total 257:55, 100 scudi paid on account by 12 July, signed off by Amato Vannini 'Can.co Deput.o'. Instrument (243r-244r): 'Die Lunæ vigesima nona Mensis Septembris' 1710, Clement XI year 10 (weekday checks); crown placed 'Super Caput Statuæ ejusdem Almæ Virginis Mariæ S.ctæ Miraculorum' by the bishop; the Latin is heavily garbled (Cremonese canons named: Maynoldi, Sforza, Cambiago, Tesauro; cardinal-legate and 'Regio Magistratu' present); followed by the 'Ordo Servandus in Coronandis Coronis aureis' and Cremona chancery authentications (244v, dated 19 Apr 1709 in one OCR copy and 26 Jul 1690 in the other). The concession date 1709-04-15 comes from the margin note 'Conceditur ac mandatur confici auream coronam Die 15 Aprilis 1709' on the conto cover at 245v (Giardini signature), assigned to Caravaggio because it sits between this dossier and the Frascati one and speaks of a single crown; medium confidence. Margin 'N. C. 26.' at 243v may be a register reference. 242v is an illegible Latin page.

rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA VIRGO « A MIRACULIS », IN AEDE LOCI « CASALBORDINO » VENERATA, TOTIUS THEATINAE ARCHIDIOECESIS PRAECIPUA PATRONA CONSTITUITUR.
incipit_latin: Mirum sane quot Templa Marialia Itala tellus, virtutis rectique cultus praecipua altrix, arcana quadam fecunditate quasi procreaverit
notes: Patron-declaration act; states in passing that the Vatican Chapter (Capitulum Vaticanum) crowned the image with a golden crown on 11 June 1899: 'quod Capitulum Vaticanum die xi mensis Iunii, anno MDCCCXCIX, inter Christifidelium acclamantium vota, aurea corona voluit redimitum'. The shrine lies in the diocese of Vasto, while the patronage granted is over the whole Archdiocese of Chieti (Theatina).

legate: Adeodatus Ioannes Piazza, S.R.E. Cardinalis, Patriarch of Venice
rubric_latin: ECCLESIA PAROECIALIS, GODII IN ARCE MANTUANAE DIOECESIS EXTANS, DEO IN HONOREM B. MARIAE V. VULGO « MADONNA DELLA SALUTE » DICATA, BASILICIS MINORIBUS ACCENSETUR.
incipit_latin: Ut pretiosissima gemma in aureo anulo sic Ecclesia, in qua pervetusta Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis sub titulo v. « Madonna della Salute » ditissimo fulget diademate
notes: Basilica Minor act recording a coronation carried out in the Pope's name: 'ditissimo fulget diademate Eidem sollemniter imposito Nostro Nomine die iv mensis Novembris superioris anni a Dilecto Filio Nostro Adeodato Ioanne S.R.E. Presbytero Cardinali Piazza, Venetiarum Patriarcha' — and later 'auctoritate Nostra, per similes Apostolicas Litteras die xxix mensis Octobris eiusdem anni sub anulo Piscatoris datas, aurea corona gemmata ... sollemniter redimita est fictilis perantiqua Imago'. 'superioris anni' relative to the act (15 Aug 1946) gives 4 Nov 1945; the enabling Apostolic Letters are dated 29 Oct 1945. Terracotta image found within the walls of the castle of Godium in 1702, popularly 'del terraglio'. Passage printed_page was 447; act begins on printed p. 445. 'Godium' is Castel Goffredo (Mantua) — identification inferred from 'Godii in arce ... in ripa Mincii ... Gonzaga Marchionum'.

rubric_latin: DE SANCTUARIO S. MARIAE AD RUPES AD VALLEM SUPPENTONIAM.
incipit_latin: Quo pietatis studium in Cristifidelium animis impensius excitarent Sanctorumque cultum omni ope proveherent, consueverunt Romani Pontifices decessores Nostri perhonorificis nominibus, privilegiis gratiisque ea loca sacra vel templa augere
notes: Motu proprio erecting the sanctuary into a minor basilica, stating in passing 'decreto Ordinis Canonicorum Basilicae Vaticanae, sacerrimo Virginis simulacro diadema ex auro gemmisque est impositum' - i.e. crowning by decree of the Vatican Chapter; no date given. Passage printed_page was 554; the act begins on printed page 553 (rubric and incipit verified in the volume text), used as aas_page. OCR reads 'Cristifidelium' for 'Christifidelium'. Country Italy inferred from Nepi/Castel Sant'Elia - unambiguous.

rubric_latin: TEMPLUM S. MARIAE VULGO " DI POZZANO ", APUD STABIAM SEU CASTRUM MARIS, TITULO BASILICAE HONESTATUR.
incipit_latin: Romanorum Pontificum Decessorum Nostrorum vestigia persequentes, sacras Aedes, quae, ante actis aetatibus erectae artisque omne genus operibus exornatae
notes: 'Ordo Canonicorum Basilicae Vaticanae anno MDCCCLXXIV, cum ingenti bonorum plausu laetitiaque, eandem Deiparae Imaginem aurea corona redimiit.' The act begins on printed p. 259 (passage printed_page is 260). Two other images in the same church (Christ crucified, St Francis of Paola) are mentioned but not said to be crowned.

act_type: Decretum Consistoriale (S. Congregatio Consistorialis) - erectio in Basilicam minorem
rubric_latin: CLAVAREN. ERECTIONIS AD DIGNITATEM BASILICAE MINORIS. Cathedralis ecclesia B. M. Virgini de Horto Clavara sacra in Basilicam minorem erigitur.
incipit_latin: Inter aedes augustae Dei Genitrici in Liguria dicatas ea sane memoratu digna est quae Clavarii existit Beatae Virgini ab Horto nuncupatae sacra
notes: Retrospective clause on printed p. 479: '... eam anno MDCXLV urbis Clavarii praesides ac finitimorum pagorum magistratus, cunctis plaudentibus, in caelestem civitatis ac totius Clavarensis regionis Praestitem delegerint, atque Vaticanum Capitulum sacram Imaginem aurea corona donandam decreverit.' Crowning decreed by the Chapter of St Peter's (Capitulum Vaticanum). Confidence medium because the year MDCXLV = 1645 is stated primarily of the patronal election, and it is only by the construction of the sentence that it also covers the Chapter's decree; a checker should verify the coronation year. Page set to 478, where the decree begins (the coronation statement is on p. 479; rubric line 'CLAVAREN. ERECTIONIS AD DIGNITATEM BASILICAE MINORIS' taken from the full volume text). OCR: 'Clavara' for 'Clavarii'/'Clavarensi', 'moHtionibus' for 'molitionibus'. Country: 'in Liguria' explicit.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 70r–73v
act_type: Chapter dossier: instrumentum donationis, lettera, supplica
legate: R.mus D. Melchior [surname garbled], canon of the Vatican Basilica, ex Cubicularius honoris of Clement XI, 'specialiter deputatus'
deputy: R.mus D. Melchior [surname garbled], canon of the Vatican Basilica, ex Cubicularius honoris of Clement XI, 'specialiter deputatus'
rubric_latin: Immagine della Madonna S.ma di Cibona, ò M.te Vrbano, Diocese di Sutri venerata nella Chiesa de PP. Eremiti del M.te Senario che habitano nel Sac. Eremo denominato di Cibona
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Infant Jesus) — 'duas Coronas aureas ... coronandi vera Simulacra ... Beat.mæ Virginis ejusq. SS.mi Infantis Jesu'. Petitioner: The Hermits of Monte Senario at the Eremo di Cibona ('Istanza ... 1690'), with an attestation letter of 'Fran.co Vesc.o di Subi.o Neri' (probably Francesco, bishop of Sutri e Nepi) dated 8 May 1690. The bishop's letter (f. 70r-71r, dated 'Stegi 8. Maggio 1690' — 'Stegi' is probably OCR for Nepi; signature 'Vesc.o di Subi.o Neri' read as 'Vescovo di Sutri e Nepi') attests the three conditions: painted c. 1462 at the expense of Agostino Chigi, alum-works contractor, for the alum-mine workers; miracles registered to no. 1223 (or 3000); given in custody to the hermits by Urban VIII in 1633; never crowned. f. 71v docket: 'Istanza Per la Coronazione della Sac. Immagine della Bma. Verg. Maria del M. Urbano Diocesi di Sut[ri] 1690' with annotations 'Suis loc. et tempore corona[bitur]' and 'Scribat S[ecreta]rio' — so the 1690 date is that of the request/deferred concession, not an explicit 'conceditur'. The instrument (f. 72r-73r) is dated 1 June 1704, Clement XI year 4, drawn up 'in mansione Cap.li eiusd. Erem.i'; it records the crowns weighed at 'centum du[o] et unius denarij aurei' and that the simulacra were carried to the church and crowned before a great multitude; accepted by 'R. P. f. Amadeus ... Rector ejusd. Eremij'; notary 'Horatius ... Suentius' (garbled). The archivist's margin note at f. 73v reads 'Instrum. Donationis Duarum Coronarum aurearum factae ... simulacro miraculoso B. M. V. ... in Ven. Eccl. Sacri Eremi RR. PP. Eremitarum ... in Terr[itorio] [T]olphae; die 18 Junij 1[7]84' — OCR gives '1784', impossible for this volume, and '18 Junij' conflicts with the instrument's 'prima Junii'; the instrument date is preferred. Country inferred from Sutri/Tolfa.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 77r–81v
