legate: Alexander (Bernardo) Casale (Casalius Coccianus Romanus), Canon of St Peter's, Referendary of both Signatures
deputy: Alexander (Bernardo) Casale (Casalius Coccianus Romanus), Canon of St Peter's, Referendary of both Signatures
rubric_latin: Decretum S. Belvedere fuori delle mura della Città di Caprarola coronata li XI. Novembre 1703
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Margin note reads 'Città di Caprarola' (OCR/archivist slip) but every document says Città di Castello; the hill is 'Villa di Caprano' / 'Collis Capsani'. Margin '(perusina)' on f.78v. Instrument dated 11 Nov 1703 (Clement XI a. III), notary Angelo Balubas Tiphernas; crowns received by Abbate Giuseppe Grasselli, perpetual curate/rector of the church; crowns weighed 54 scudi d'oro in oro. Relazione says the crowning took place under Bishop Eustachi. Endorsement on f.81v gives '1.ª 7br. 1703' (1 Sept 1703), possibly the concession/decree date, but its function is unclear so concession_date left null. Conto on f.79r (dated '15 9bre') signed 'Bernardo Casale Can.co Red.re dep.to' — the instrument names the deputy 'Alexander Casalius'; both readings kept.

legate: Andreas Carolus Ferrari, S.R.E. Cardinalis, Archiepiscopus Mediolanensis
rubric_latin: ARCHIPRESBYTERALE TEMPLUM, CIVITATIS AC DIOECESIS COMENSIS INTRA FINES, IN HONOREM S. GEORGII MARTYRIS DEO DICATUM, TITULO BASILICAE MINORIS CONDECORATUR.
incipit_latin: Comensi in civitate ac dioecesi exstat antiquum templum archipresbyterale in honorem Sancti Georgii Martyris Deo dicatum, quod Sancti Euthychii Episcopi Comensis titulo etiam honestatur
notes: Basilica Minor grant. Attestation: 'Nostrae Dominae a Sacro Corde simulacrum, quod eadem in ecclesia custoditur, magni pretii coronis redimitum, quas nomine Decessoris Nostri Benedicti Pp. XV, pretiosorum quoque lapidum quibus ipsae coronae sunt contextae munifici donatoris, Sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae Cardinalis recolendae memoriae Andreas Ferrari, Mediolanensium Archiepiscopus uti Legatus imposuit'. OCR reads 'Andreas Perrari' and 'redimitimi'; repaired. Crowned in the name of Benedict XV (so 1914-1921, Ferrari d. Feb. 1921); no date given. Passage printed_page 327, but the act begins on p. 326 (verified in the volume text).

rubric_latin: ECCLESIA B. M. VIRGINIS AD NIVES, IN OPPIDO CUGLIERI, DIOECESIS BOSANENSIS, BASILICAE MINORIS TITULO AC PRIVILEGIIS HONESTATUR.
incipit_latin: Vestigiis Romanorum Pontificum decessorum Nostrorum insistentes, sacras catholici orbis aedes, quae vetustate, monumentis artium et antiqua populorum religione excellant
notes: Basilica Minor act citing the coronation: the Chapter of the Vatican Basilica decreed the golden diadem on 4 December 1892 ('die iv mensis decembris anno MDCCCXCII') and the rite was performed on 5 August 1893 ('die v mensis augusti anno MDCCCXCIII'); the passage's printed_page is 410 but the act begins on printed page 409, used here. Rubric OCR 'ECCLESIA EU M. VIRGINIS' repaired to 'ECCLESIA B. M. VIRGINIS'. Marble statue ('marmoreum eius simulacrum, auro gemmisque ornatum').

rubric_latin: TITULO ET PRIVILEGIIS BASILICAE MINORIS CONDECORATUR ECCLESIA PAROECIALIS B. M. V. GRATIARUM, CIVITATIS « ESTE », IN DIOECESI PATAVINA.
incipit_latin: Surgit in civitate Este, dioecesis Patavinae intra limites, ecclesia Deo dicata in honorem Beatae Mariae Virginis sub Gratiarum invocatione
notes: 'Ipsa sacra imago ex decreto Vaticanae Basilicae Capituli diei XV mensis decembris anni MDCCCXXII, pretioso diademate redimita refulget.' The date given (15 December 1822) is that of the Vatican Chapter decree, not necessarily of the crowning, so coronation_date left null. Image said to have been brought from Constantinople in 1408.

rubric_latin: BEATA VIRGO MARIA « A BONO IESU », VULGO « MADONNA DEL BUON GESÙ » APPELLATA, UNA CUM S. IOANNE BAPTISTA, PRAECURSORE DOMINI ET MARTYRE, PATRONA CAELESTIS CIVITATIS ET DIOECESIS FABRIANENSIS CONSTITUITUR.
incipit_latin: Magno afficimur gaudio cum fere quotidie Nobis compertum sit vota, quae in indicendo Anno Mariano primo exeunte saeculo a definito dogmate Immaculatae Conceptionis
notes: Clause: « Capitulum Vaticanum ... aureis coronis tam Divini Infantis quam eius Sanctissimae Matris capita redimiri sua auctoritate decreverit : quod die VIII Septembris, anno MDCCCXCVIII feliciter factum est ». Both the Infant Jesus and the Virgin were crowned in the one rite. The image is a painting kept « in suo parvo sed ornatissimo sacello », not named. Coronation clause on printed page 366; the act begins on printed page 365, cited here as aas_page.

legate: Michael Lega, S.R.E. Cardinalis
rubric_latin: TITULO ET PRIVILEGIIS BASILICAE MINORIS DITATUR ECCLESIA CATHEDRALIS CIVITATIS AC DIOECESIS FAVENTINAE.
incipit_latin: « Faventia fidelis » : conciso hoc uno dicto iure meritoque appellanda atque, prout nomen ipsum suadere videtur
notes: Basilica Minor act; coronation attested in passing: 'cuius Imaginem rec. mem. faventinus Sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae Cardinalis Michael Lega, proximi Decessoris Nostri nomine, aurea corona, anno MCMXXXI, sollemniter redimivit' — i.e. crowned 1931 by Cardinal Michele Lega in the name of Pius XI. Passage printed_page was 542; act begins on printed p. 541. Vernacular title supplied as the Italian form of 'Maria gratiarum'.

legate: Fodianus Ordinarius (Iosephus Lenotti, Archiepiscopus Fodianus, was the petitioner and is charged to impose the crown 'Nostro nomine et auctoritate')
rubric_latin: Sinitur pretioso diademate redimiri imago Beatae Mariae Virginis vulgo Iconavetere nuncupata, quae in cathedrali templo metropolitanae Ecclesiae Fodianae exstat.
incipit_latin: Cum ducentesimus et quinquagesimus feliciter recurreret annus impletus ex quo fideles Fodiani mariali, ut fertur, prodigio sunt ditati
notes: Opens 'Ad futuram rei memoriam' (not 'Ad perpetuam'). The act itself attests an EARLIER coronation of the same image: 'secundum etiam revolveretur saeculum postquam imago Beatae Mariae Virginis vulgo Iconavetere appellata a Petriano Canonicorum Collegio coronata est' - i.e. the second centenary of a crowning by the Vatican Chapter, so c. 1781; the exact year is not given. Occasion also the 250th year since the Marian prodigy at Foggia. Country Italy inferred from the see of Foggia (Fodiana); not stated in the act. Coronation day left to the Ordinary's choice. Confirmed in the volume indices at pp. 757 and 776.

legate: Angelus Iosephus S. R. E. Presb. Cardinalis Roncalli, Venetiarum Patriarcha
rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA V. « DOMINA NOSTRA A GRATIIS IN FOLGARIA » PRAECIPUA CAELESTIS PATRONA ELIGITUR OMNIUM SOLEIS OBLONGIS PER NIVES PROLABENTIUM EX ITALIA, QUI « SCIATORI » VULGO APPELLANTUR.
incipit_latin: Quae « abiit in montana » (Cf. Luc. I, 39), castis visceribus portans Divinum Redemptorem, Beatae Mariae Virginis honori recte constituta sunt editis in iugis vel alpinis camporum spatiis domicilia religionis
notes: Patron-declaration act; attests 'Mariano, qui proxime praeteriit, Anno; quo vertente Deiparae Imago eo in Templo exculta, auctoritate Petriani Canonicorum Collegii, per ... Cardinalem Roncalli, Venetiarum Patriarcham, aurea est diademate redimita.' Crowning was by authority of the Vatican Chapter (not a papal legation), executed by Card. Roncalli during the Marian Year that had just ended (Dec 1953 - Dec 1954); coronation year given as 1954 by inference from 'Anno Mariano qui proxime praeteriit' - verify exact date. Rubric OCR reads 'POLGARIA' (= Folgaria). Act begins on printed page 379.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 268r–289v
act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, relazione
legate: Mons. Guido del Palagio (de Balagio / del Baglio), Patrizio Romano, canonico della Basilica Vaticana, Referendario di Segnatura
deputy: Mons. Guido del Palagio (de Balagio / del Baglio), Patrizio Romano, canonico della Basilica Vaticana, Referendario di Segnatura
rubric_latin: Instrum Donationis Duar. Coronar. aurear. valoris 409 ... imaginib. miraculosis B. M. V. de Planchis, et Pueri Iesu existent. in Eccl. ... Societatis sub invocat. eiusd. ssmae Virginis de Planchis, et S.ti Leonardi Civitatis Fulginei p. die XIV. mensis Majj 1716
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), 'all'Imperiale', valued 409:81 scudi. Petitioner: Confraternita / Archiconfraternita della Madonna del Pianto e S. Leonardo di Foligno (Governatore Francesco Silvestri, Guardiani Filippo Giusti and Vincenzo Bussaroni, 1704; Governatore Giovanni Battista Marcelli, 1713). Image is a dressed wooden statue of the Virgin seated with the Child (attestation of 9 Aug 1704, notary Giovanni Scarpellini, with a drawing 'accluso' and notes on the silver crown/star at f. 272v). Documents: sworn attestation of origin and miracles (earthquake of 14 Jan 1703) 1704 = 'other'; an undated letter (f. 271r) asking the Canons for a 'dilazione' so the feast of coronation could wait for the new church ('dentro il Mese di Mag. 1702', '1703') - implies the concession predates 1704 but no decree date is given, hence concession_date null; mandate to Giardini (f. 277r) 'p. la Ma.da SS.ma della Terr.a di Foligno'; conto Giardini 20 May 1713 (OCR 'Fulignio', later dates '1623' = 1713); Latin instrumentum of donation Actum in the Cathedral of Foligno 14 May 1713 (Sunday), attested by the bishop 'Aloisius Malvitius Fontana' 22 May 1713; relazione headed (OCR) 'il 23: Maggio 1723 da Monsig.r Ill.mo Guido del Baglio' - read 1713; relazione text fixes the day as 'quatordici del Mese di Maggio', Sunday after vespers, the day after 'Sabbato 23 [=13]'. Margin note 272v adds 'Dicembre' after 1713, unexplained. The relazione runs on past f. 285r. Piratello letters (ff. 273r-275r) are interleaved inside this folio span. | Range opens mid-way through the Italian relazione of the ceremony (begins before pb 673); the deputy is called only 'Mons.r Ill.mo Incoronante' and is never named in these pages. Relazione: Saturday 23 May, first vespers sung by 'Mon Sig: Malavicini' Bishop of Foligno (name OCR-uncertain), coronation performed the following Sunday after vespers in the Cathedral of S. Feliciano, statues of Mother and Child crowned, De profundis for Count Sforza, procession the following Tuesday. 23 May fell on a Saturday only in 1716 among nearby years, so coronation = Sunday 24 May 1716; the margin note's instrument date 'XIV. mensis Majj 1716' is probably OCR for XXIV. 'de Planchis' = de Planctu (Madonna del Pianto). 'Caps. B 9' probably 'Caps. 29'. Only margin notes survive for ff. 287r-289v; f.289v also carries the head 'Conto ... delle Corone d'Oro' with signature 'Gio: Giardin Argentiere' (silversmith's account, text not transcribed).

image_title_vernacular: Madonna di Follina (Santa Maria Assunta / Annunciazione)
rubric_latin: TITULUS BASILICAE MINORIS CONFERTUR ECCLESIAE SEU SANCTUARIO ANNUNCIATIONIS B. M. V., OPPIDI « FOLLINA », DIOECESIS CENETENSIS.
incipit_latin: Ampla ac pervetusta Cisterciensium Fratrum abbatia, decimo secundo labente saeculo fundata, exstat intra fines dioecesis Cenetensis, in civitate vulgo Follina
notes: Basilica Minor act granted on the occasion of a FUTURE coronation: 'auspicatam occasionem nactus coronationis dictae prodigiosae imaginis quae ex decreto Basilicae Vaticanae Capituli proximo septembri mense aureo diademate sollemni pompa augebitur' - to be crowned by decree of the Vatican Chapter in September 1921 (day not given; letter dated 10 August 1921). Image is a marble carving of the Virgin with the Child Jesus. Act begins on printed page 470 (passage printed_page is 471).

act_type: Litterae Apostolicae (Breve, sub annulo Piscatoris) - erectio in Basilicam minorem
rubric_latin: Ecclesia SS. Rosarii B. M. V. oppidi Fontanellato dioecesis Parmensis erigitur in Basilicam minorem.
incipit_latin: Extat intra fines Parmensis dioeceseos in oppido, cui nomen vulgo Fontanellato, sacra aedes Deo in honorem Sacratissimo Rosarii Beatae Mariae Virginis dicata
notes: Retrospective clause: 'in qua vetus ipsius Deiparae Virginis colitur simulacrum, clarum prodigiis atque aurea corona gemmisque distincta anno 1660 redimitum.' Confidence lowered to medium because the text does NOT say by whose authority the crown was conferred (no mention of the Vatican Chapter or of a papal indult), so the papal-authority element is unattested here; a checker should verify. OCR: 'distincta' for 'distinctum'/'distinct[a corona]'; 'honorii!centias' for 'honorificentias'. Country derived from 'dioecesis Parmensis' / 'ex Aemilia ... ex aliis Italiae regionibus'.

legate: Eugenius Card. Tosi, Archiepiscopus Mediolanensis
rubric_latin: AD EM.UM P. D. EUGENIUM, TIT. SS. SILVESTRI ET MARTINI, S. R. E. PRESB. CARD. TOSI ARCHIEPISCOPUM MEDIOLANENSEM, QUEM DELIGIT LEGATUM SUUM AD CORONAS IMPONENDAS INFANTI IESU ET BEATAE VIRGINI DE FONTANELLATO, IN DIOECESI PARMENSI.
incipit_latin: Quod Sanctuarii de Fontanellato laus ac fama non modo in dioecesis Parmensis totiusque Aemiliae finibus percrebrescit, sed etiam apud exteras gentes
notes: Single statue group: crowns for both the Virgin and the Infant Jesus she carries ('coronas ... Virgini de Fontanellato et Infanti Iesu, quem Ipsa in ulnis sustinet, veluti manibus Nostris imponas'), the Pope himself blessing the crowns beforehand. Solemnities set for May 1925 ('sacris sollemnibus mense maio Parmae habendis'), hence coronation_date 1925. The act also records earlier crownings in 1660 and 1771 ('quam annis MDCLX et MDCCLXXI factum est'). Vernacular title supplied from the place name; the act gives only 'Virgo de Fontanellato'.

image_title_vernacular: Madonna di Capocroce (B. V. detta di Capo croce)
citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 246r–256v.[03.mn.0000]
act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, other, relazione, stampa
legate: Faustino Crispolti, Canon of the Vatican Basilica, Referendary and Auditor of Card. Spinola (deputed by Chapter 22 Oct 1713)
deputy: Faustino Crispolti, Canon of the Vatican Basilica, Referendary and Auditor of Card. Spinola (deputed by Chapter 22 Oct 1713)
rubric_latin: Instru. Donationis duar. Coronar. aurear. ... fact. Imaginibus miraculosis B. M. V. et Pueri Jesu d. S. Maria di Capo d'Oca in civitate Tusculana die 20. xbr. 1713 — Caps. 39. fasc. 329
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Dossier contents: notarial extract of the 1703 Apostolic Visitation of Frascati (Abp. F. M. de Rubeis) describing the mural image 'B. M. V. Puerum gestantis in muro depicta' in S. Mariæ Capitis Crucis of the Theatines, translated 5 May 1613, extract dated 18 Dec 1709 (246r-v); Giardini conto for two imperial crowns, 111 scudi of gold, total 228:30, paid 215 scudi from 2 Nov 1713 to 11 Oct 1714 (247r); instrument of consignment by notary Pietro Ignazio Lelli, Frascati, 28 Oct 1713 (248r-249r), archivist summary at 249v (OCR reads 'Capo d'Oca' and '20. xbr.' for Capocroce / 28 8br); conto cover with 'Decretum 11 9bris 1709' (250v) and filing note '1709 51 / Frascati de' PP. Teatini' (251v); relazione of the coronation (252r-253v); engravings by Giovan Franceschini 'Vera Effigie della Miracolosa Vergine ... detta di Capocroce' (254r; the 1813 reprint at 256r); 1819 commemorative inscription 'MEMORIAE ET POSTERITATI' recording the crown given 'IV KAL. NOVEMBRIS' 1713, copied by Mons. D'Achille 9 Oct 1855 (254v-255v). Coronation date: relazione and instrument give Saturday 28 Oct 1713; one engraving caption reads '11. di Settembre 1713' (probably OCR/engraver variant). The crowns were fixed on the images by P. Filippo Maria Trigoni/Triconi, Theatine. Petitioner not stated in range (Theatine fathers, Vicar Guglielmo della Valle, received the crowns). '1709 51' / 'origine N. 51' at 251v may be a further filing reference.

image_title_vernacular: Madonna di Capocroce (B. V. detta di Capo croce)
rubric_latin: AD DIGNITATEM ET HONOREM BASILICAE MINORIS EVEHITUR ECCLESIA SANCTAE MARIAE A CRUCE DIOECESIS CREMENSIS.
incipit_latin: Sedes religionis Marialis praecipua dioecesis Cremensis perhibetur esse templum Sanctae Mariae a Cruce, multiplici sane laude commendatum
notes: Generic retrospective mention: « Suis etiam muneribus Romani Pontifices hoc pietatis domicilium auxerunt, simulacrum Beatae Mariae Virginis aurea corona redimiri sinentes, peculiares illi tribuentes Indulgentias ... ». No date, pope or minister given. The text names only the diocese (« intra fines Cremensis dioecesis »), not the town, so locality left null; Italy is explicit (« publicis Italiae monumentis annumeraretur »). Vernacular title is the Italian form of the Latin dedication.

legate: Thomas Pius S. R. E. Card. Boggiani, Archbishop of Genoa
rubric_latin: AD THOMAM PIUM S. R. E. PRESB. CARD. BOGGIANI, ARCHIEPISCOPUM IANUENSEM, QUI DELEGATUR A B. P. UT EIUS NOMINE SIMULACRUM DEIPARAE A VINEIS AUREA CORONA REDIMIAT ET BENEDICTIONEM IMPERTIAT CUM INDULGENTIA PLENARIA.
incipit_latin: Quae civitatis istius, pastorali studio tuo commissae, propius intersint, ea planum est sic ad Nos pertinere
notes: Benedict XV delegates Card. Boggiani to crown the marble image in his name ('hoc tibi munus delegamus, ut, nomine Nostro, et effigiem Deiparae a Vineis aurea, quam memoravimus, corona redimias'). Coronation date derived from 'ea in diem primum ac vicesimum vertentis mensis, qui dies Deiparae a Vineis sacer est ... indixistis' in a letter dated 1 November 1920, hence 21 November 1920 - verify. This is the fourth centennial crowning: Abp Orazio Spinola first crowned the image in 1616 ('anno MDCXVI ... diademate primum ornasse'), with the rite to be repeated every hundred years; the 1916 centenary was deferred because of the war. Benedict XV, baptized in this parish church, donated the golden crown.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 177r–177v
rubric_latin: Capitulo Ecclesię Metropolitanę Januensi ... Sanctę Imaginis Beatiss.mę Virginis asservatę in Sacello eiusdem Metropolitanę, quę colitur sub Invocatione Sanctę Marię Liberatricis Auream Coronam eidem concessa fuit
notes: Crowns: one ('Auream Coronam eidem concessa fuit'). Petitioner: Archbishop, Senate and Chapter of the Metropolitan church of Genoa (Archiepiscopo, Senatui et Capitulo Ecclesię Metropolitanę Januensi). Single leaf: certificate of the Chapter secretary (Alexander Chiavelli[?] Can. & Secret.), dated 22 Nov 1742, attesting that in the extraordinary capitular congregation of 9 Sept 1742 the gold crown was conceded, 'habendam tamen suis loco et tempore et pro nunc faciendam sumptibus praesentium' (crown to be made for now at the petitioners' expense). Margin note reads '113 175' and '~ S. Maria in Vico ~', which does not match the text; f.177v margin 'R. 118'. 'Januensi' (Genoa) is the OCR reading; note that the following dossier concerns the Palermo Cathedral statue 'S. Maria Libera Inferni', whose printed history glosses the name as 'Liberatrice dal Purgatorio' - it is possible this certificate actually concerns Palermo (Metropolitan church, Senate, chapel, immemorial cult) and 'Januensi' is an OCR error; cannot be verified. The label leaf f.178v ('351', 'Decretum 23 Febr. 1699') sits between this record and the Palermo dossier; its attribution is uncertain.

rubric_latin: Titulo ac privilegiis Basilicae Minoris Sanctuarium B. Mariae Virg. vulgo « dei Suffragio » in oppido vulgo « Grotte di Castro », dioecesis Faliscodunensis, sacrum, decoratur.
incipit_latin: Christifidelium concursibus frequentato templum Beatae Mariae Virginis, vulgo « dei Suffragio » nuncupatae, quod in oppido « Grotte di Castro », uti appellant, intra Faliscodunensis dioecesis fines est positum.
notes: Basilica Minor act; coronation attested in passing: 'simulacrum hoc mariale anno MDCCXXVIII, auctoritate Petriani Collegii Canonicorum, aureo diademate est redimitum' (OCR 'redimitimi'), the anniversary being kept every sixteenth year. Incipit reproduces OCR 'frequentato' (probably 'frequentatur'). 'Faliscodunensis' identified as Montefiascone (the same volumes pair it with Cornetana and Aquipendiensis); today part of the diocese of Viterbo - verify. Rubric spells the town 'Grotte di Castro', the dispositive clause 'Grotte del Castro'.

rubric_latin: Beata Maria Virgo « della Porta » appellata principalis Patrona urbis episcopalis et totius dioecesis Guastallensis, una cum Sancto Francisco Assisiensi, Patrono aeque principali, constituitur.
incipit_latin: Porta caeli ab Ecclesia merito praedicatur Beata Maria Virgo: hanc enim si sequuntur in cursu vitae terrenae, homines metam feliciter contingunt
notes: Patronage act; coronation attested in passing: 'Sanctus Pius Pp. X, Decessor Noster, concessit, ut imago aurea corona, suo nomine et auctoritate, redimiretur' - no year. The image, originally on a city gate, began to work wonders on 7 February 1693. OCR prints 'delia Porta' for 'della Porta' throughout (repaired here). Country inferred from Guastalla and the Italian vernacular title - not stated in the act.

rubric_latin: BASILICAE MINORIS HONORIBUS AC PRIVILEGIIS AFFICITUR ECCLESIA BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS NEMORENSIS, SEU V. « MADONNA DEL BOSCO », IN OPPIDO « IMBERSAGO », MEDIOLANENSIS ARCHIDIOECESIS.
incipit_latin: Fortiter suaviterque ad ineundas religionis semitas immo et sacerdotii Divinam Misericordiam Nos a teneris annis impulisse, iuvat nunc grato animo meminisse
notes: « quod Nosmet Ipsi, inter Patres Cardinales asciti ac Venetiarum Patriarcham agentes, anno MCMLIV, pro desideratissimo Hildefonso Alfredo S. R. E. Presbytero Cardinali Schuster, tunc Archiepiscopo Mediolanensi, graviter infirmo, aurea corona sollemni ritu coronavimus. » John XXIII crowned it himself, but in 1954, as Cardinal Patriarch of Venice, standing in for the ailing Card. Schuster — i.e. before his election, so classify with care.

rubric_latin: E.mo P. D. Ioanni Baptistae S. R. E. Cardinali Montini, Archiepiscopo Mediolanensi, qui in oppido v. « Imbersago » interfuit sollemnibus, quibus statua aenea Ioanni Pp. XXIII posita est in sacra Aede B. Mariae Virg. v. « Madonna del Bosco » appellatae.
incipit_latin: Con soave pensiero l'animo si volge al Santuario della Madonna del Bosco, che soffuse su la Nostra infanzia un ineffabile sorriso di cielo
notes: Letter in Italian to Card. Montini. John XXIII recalls: 'il 29 agosto 1954, con la cerimonia della solenne incoronazione della sacra effigie, ivi venerata, che Ci fu dato di compiere in nome e per procura del Cardinale Arcivescovo Schuster'. IMPORTANT for a checker: the writer (then Patriarch of Venice, not yet Pope) performed the crowning as proxy for Cardinal Schuster, Archbishop of Milan; the text does NOT state papal or Vatican Chapter authority for the coronation, so 'papal_personal_coronation' is used only in the literal sense that the reigning Pope personally performed it. Rubric OCR reads « Imfoersago » — repaired to « Imbersago ». Diocese (Milan) inferred from the addressee and from Card. Schuster; country inferred from Brianza/Lombardy. The letter opens on printed page 850; the coronation clause falls on page 851.

rubric_latin: E.mo P. D. Ioanni Baptistae S. R. E. Cardinali Montini, Archiepiscopo Mediolanensi, qui in oppido v. « Imbersago » interfuit sollemnibus, quibus statua aenea Ioanni Pp. XXIII posita est in sacra Aede B. Mariae Virg. v. « Madonna del Bosco » appellatae.
notes: The Pope recalls 'la cerimonia della solenne incoronazione della sacra effigie, ivi venerata, che Ci fu dato di compiere in nome e per procura del Cardinale Arcivescovo Schuster' on 29 August 1954 — i.e. the crowning was performed by Angelo Roncalli (then Patriarch of Venice, not yet Pope) as proxy for Cardinal Ildefonso Schuster, Archbishop of Milan, the day before Schuster's death. Hence retrospective_attestation, not papal_personal_coronation. OCR of the rubric reads 'Imfoersago'; read as 'Imbersago'. Act begins on printed page 850; passage page 851. Body in Italian, no Latin incipit.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 257r–275r
act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, relazione
legate: Mons. Giovanni Andrea Ricci, canonico di S. Pietro
deputy: Mons. Giovanni Andrea Ricci, canonico di S. Pietro
rubric_latin: Instro della Coronat.ne di due Corone d'oro fatta all'Imagino della SS.ma Vergine, e Bambino Giesù detta del Piratello esistente nella Chiesa dei PP. del T. ord.e di S. Fran.co fuori della Città d'Imola
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Petitioner: the Franciscans of the Third Order (P. Generale Paolo Lombardini; P. Maestro F. Elia) and other superiors of the church, who requested the crowns in advance. Giardini conto (257r): two crowns weighing 37 scudi 2 den. of gold, worked with foliage and cherub heads, total 83 scudi, settled at 78 scudi; the sum was advanced by the General of the Franciscan Third Order to be refunded by the Chapter 'quando avvinarà il tempo e il Luogo nel quale doveano darsi dette Corone'. Conto cover with 'Decretum die Lunae 2 9brjs 1711' (258v; 2 Nov 1711 was a Monday). Payment order by Amato Vannini, Canon Dean, 10 Dec 1713 ('come a ciò deputato', probably as the Chapter's deputy for the crowns rather than the crowning deputy) and Giardini's receipt dated Dec 1713 (259r). No coronation or instrument in range; the dossier ends at the last page of the batch, so it likely continues. OCR spells the town 'Immola' / 'Imola'. | Dossier is interleaved with the Foligno one: Piratello material at ff. 257r-267r.02 (conto Giardini 78 scudi for the two crowns, paid 10 Dec 1713 by the Franciscan Third Order general; margin 'Decretum die Lunae 2 9brjs 1711' on the conto sheet, taken as the concession decree - 2 Nov 1711 was a Monday, but the decree could instead concern the payment; instrument of quittance 'Actum Imolae in Platea Publica' 15 Aug 1714 = 'Die Mercurij ... Decima quinta mensis Augusti', Wednesday, consistent; relazione of the triduo 14-16 Aug 1714 with the crowning on Assumption Day; two copies of Card. Gozzadini's thank-you letter, OCR-dated '9bre 1712', surely 1714) and again at ff. 273r-275r (Ricci's covering letter 'Imola 19 Agosto 1714'; archivist note at 274v; margin fragment at 275r). OCR gives the archivist's head at 261v as 'li 25 Ag.to 1714' and 274v 'Sotto li 29 Ag.to 1714' - read 15 and 19. Ricci's deputation is OCR-dated '5. marzo 1723' (read 1714). Image: painting on terracotta venerated since 1488. Cardinal named 'Forzadori' in OCR = Gozzadini. f. 267v.01 is an unrelated misfiled 1618 supplica about a canon of Cosenza. f. 275r also carries a 1717 order to pay Giardini for 'l'ultima Corona d'oro' naming no image.

image_title_vernacular: Maria Ausiliatrice (Madonna del soccorso dei Cristiani)
rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA V. SUB TITULO « AUXILIUM CHRISTIANORUM » IN INSULA S. GEORGII, VENETIARUM PATRIARCHATUS, VENERATA, EIUSDEM INSULAE PATRONA CAELESTIS PROCLAMATUR.
incipit_latin: Marianae pietatis ac disciplinae monasticae sedes pervetus et admodum insignis in Venetiarum insula exstare perhibetur, quae a Sancto Georgio nomen accepit
notes: « ... atque, quod diximus, simulacrum anno MDCCCLXXXXIII aureo diademate sollemni ritu esse decoratum » = 1893. Crowning authority/minister not named. The statue was placed in the church on the 25th anniversary of Lepanto. Vernacular title is my rendering of the Latin « Auxilium Christianorum »; not given in the text.

image_title_vernacular: Maria Santissima della Neve del Monte Sirino
rubric_latin: Memoriae proditur Ioannem Paulum PP. II coronavisse imaginem beatae Mariae Virginis, quae titulo « Maria Santissima della Neve del Monte Sirino » invocata Lacuneruli colitur.
incipit_latin: Oblata occasione Audientiae Generalis habitae in area ante Basilicam Vaticanam sancti Petri die xx mensis Septembris hoc anno Magni Iubilaei MM, perquam libenter excipientes preces Nobis exhibitas...
notes: Retrieved from the act itself; two batch passages are volume indices (chronological index p. 904 and 'Index rerum analyticus' p. 949) which both point here. Rubric and opening on p. 848, Datum on p. 849. The act also attests an earlier coronation of the same image a century before, 'de mandato Leonis XIII' (c. 1900). Country not stated; inferred from 'Lucano agro civitatis Lacuneruli' (Lagonegro, Basilicata).

rubric_latin: ECCLESIA METROPOLITANA LANCIANENSIS TITULO BASILICAE MINORIS AUGETUR.
incipit_latin: Conspicua templa Dei, quae non minus vetustate ac molis amplitudine quam artis operibus et eximia imprimis fidelium religione prae ceteris excellant
notes: Basilica Minor elevation; crowning attested in passing: 'pervetus B. M. V. figulinum simulacrum, usque ab anno MDCCCXXXIII ex Capituli vaticani decreto aurea corona redimitum'. OCR 'tempia' repaired to 'templa' in the incipit. In the OCR the act body is interrupted by an intervening Epistola (pp. 250); the 'Datum ... die v Februarii MCMIX' belongs to this act, the earlier 'die xviii Septembris MCMVIII' to the preceding act I.

rubric_latin: Titulo ac privilegiis Basilicae Minoris ecclesia Beatae Mariae Virginis « a Catena » in oppido Lauriniano, intra Cosentinae archidioecesis fines, decoratur.
incipit_latin: Praeclara sedes pietatis marianae perhibetur esse sacrarium Beatae Mariae Virginis « a Catena », qua oppidum Laurinianum, archidioecesis Cosentina, quin etiam tota Bruttiorum regio ... aluntur ac nobilitantur
notes: Basilica Minor act; coronation attested in passing: 'imago, auctoritate Canonicorum Collegii Petrianae Basilicae Vaticanae, sollemniter aureo diademate redimita', no year given. Image dated to 1301, showing the Virgin with the Divine Infant holding a chain. 'oppidum Laurinianum' read as Laurignano (Calabria) - verify; country from 'tota Bruttiorum regio, quam Calabriam vulgo appellant'. Vernacular title (Madonna della Catena) not given in the act, so left null.

rubric_latin: TEMPLUM B. M. VIRGINIS VULGO " DEL PILASTRELLO " PROPE LENDINARAM ADRIENSIS DIOECESEOS AD DIGNITATEM BASILICAE MINORIS EVEHITUR.
incipit_latin: Traditum a Romanis Pontificibus Praedecessoribus Nostris, morem servantes, templa Dei, quae magno avitae pietatis studio circumfusa, singulari Christifidelium frequentia celebrantur
notes: 'simulacrum ipsum ab Antistitibus Adriensibus bis antea redimitum, anno demum millesimo nongentesimo sexto, ex Capituli Vaticani decreto, coronis aureis decoraretur' - i.e. crowned twice earlier by bishops of Adria, then in 1906 by decree of the Vatican Chapter. OCR 'tempia' repaired to 'templa'. Diocese is today Adria-Rovigo.

image_title_vernacular: B. V. di Leuca (Santa Maria di Leuca, 'de Finibus Terrae')
citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, f. 211v
rubric_latin: Breue relat.ne dell'antichità di Leuca nella Japigia e del celibre santuario della B. V. det- ta prisco/ Terre
notes: Named only in an archivist's wrapper heading at f. 211v: 'Breve relatione dell'antichità di Leuca nella Japigia e del celebre santuario della B. V. detta [de Finibus] Terrae [OCR 'prisco/ Terre'], con una lettera di Mons.r Vesc.o di Verona, scusando non poter andar à Coronar d.a B. a causa de sospetti di peste', with margin 'Descrit.a a fo: 54'. No Leuca document is present in this range; the letter of the bishop of Verona belongs to the Tersatto dossier, and the Leuca relation is apparently filed at fol. 54. Title reading 'de Finibus Terrae' is an inference from the OCR fragment; emitted only so the cross-reference is not lost.

legate: Petrus Card. Gasparri
rubric_latin: AD EM.UM P. D. PETRUM, TIT. SANCTI LAURENTII IN LUCINA, S. R. E. PRESB. CARDINALEM GASPARRI, A NEGOTIIS PUBLICIS ADMINISTRUM, QUEM LEGATUM MITTIT AD TRANSVEHENDAM LAURETUM BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS NOVAM ICONEM, A SE BENEDICTAM AUREOQUE DIADEMATE REDIMITAM.
incipit_latin: Norunt omnes quo maerore affectus sit orbis catholicus, cum, haud ita pridem, Lauretana aede ardescente, imago illa augustissima Beatae Mariae Virginis penitus deleta est
notes: The new statue made after the 1921 fire: 'cum Ipsi simulacrum novum Mariae et Iesu diademate aureo ditaverimus, tum idem sollemni ritu benedictum coronavimus' - Pius XI crowned it himself in Rome before 17 Aug 1922. Card. Gasparri is deputed as Legate only to convey the image to Loreto, not to crown it. Country inferred from Loreto/Lauretum (unambiguous); diocese not named in the act.

rubric_latin: AD VENERABILES FRATRES PATRIARCHAS, PRIMATES, ARCHIEPISCOPOS, EPISCOPOS, ALIOSQUE LOCORUM ORDINARIOS PACEM ET COMMUNIONEM CUM APOSTOLICA SEDE HABENTES: DE PACE CHRISTI IN REGNO CHRISTI QUAERENDA.
incipit_latin: Ubi arcano Dei consilio ac nutu Nos, qui nullis sane meritis commendaremur, ad hanc et veritatis cathedram et caritatis evecti sumus
notes: Encyclical 'Ubi arcano Dei consilio', which begins on printed p. 673; the coronation reference is on p. 675 (the passage page): 'venerabile ipsius simulacrum, apud Nos affabre refectum, Nostrisque manibus et consecratum et corona redimitum, restituendum curavimus'. Rubric and incipit taken from p. 673 of the same volume text. Same image as AAS 14 (1922) 544. Country inferred (Loreto).

rubric_latin: AD R. P. D. ALPHONSUM ANDREOLI, EPISCOPUM RECINETENSEM ET LAURETANUM, QUINQUAGESIMO PLENO ANNO AB INITO SACERDOTIO.
incipit_latin: Cum allatum ad Nos sit, quinquagesimum sacerdotii natalem a te propediem actum iri, placet in partem venire, ut aequum est, gaudii laetitiaeque tuae
notes: Act VIII begins on printed p. 215 (the passage page marker is 216). Attests in passing: 'populi pietas in novam Virginis Effigiem, quam Nosmet ipsi lustravimus et corona redimivimus'. Coronation year 1922 taken from the parallel acts AAS 14 (1922) 544 and 675, not stated here; country inferred (Loreto).

rubric_latin: TEMPLUM IN HONOREM B. MARIAE V. IN CAELUM ASSUMPTAE DEO CONSECRATUM, IN OPPIDO « LUGO » IMOLENSIS DIOECESIS HONORIBUS BASILICAE MINORIS INSIGNITUR.
incipit_latin: Templi, honori Beatae Mariae Virginis Caelo receptae sacri et in oppido « Lugo », intra fines Imolensis dioecesis, constituti, magna est, ut accepimus, religio atque antiquitas
notes: Basilica Minor elevation; attests 'Pius Pp. IX, Decessor Noster, olim loci illius Episcopus, imaginem, tot laudibus ornatam, anno MDCCCLVI, aureo diademate iussit redimiri' — i.e. crowned by order of Pius IX in 1856. The image was translated to the new church in 1943 ('anno MCMXLIII', OCR 'MCMXL i n').

rubric_latin: SANCTUARIUM BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS DE MISERICORDIA IN DIOECESI MACERATENSI TITULO AC PRIVILEGIIS BASILICAE MINORIS HONESTATUR.
incipit_latin: Anno Domini 1447, mortifera grassante pestilentia, Maceratensis urbis cives Virginem Mariam, sub titulo Misericordiae, civitatis Patronam vocarunt
notes: Basilica Minor act granted on the approaching bicentenary of the coronation: 'eidemque die 24 mensis augusti anno 1721, ex decreto Capituli Patriarchalis Vaticanae Basilicae, aureum diadema donatum impositumque fuit'. A silver crown had been offered by the townsmen in 1496 (not a papal coronation). Rubric OCR 'MACERATECI' repaired to 'MACERATENSI'. The act begins on printed page 305 (passage printed_page is 306).

rubric_latin: Titulus ac privilegia Basilicae Minoris cathedrali ecclesiae Materanensi tribuuntur.
incipit_latin: Mateola, antiqua regum sedes, urbs rerum gestarum memoria illustris, praeclarior vero religione, quam priscis acceptam temporibus per hominum aetates impigre coluit, egregium pietatis domicilium merito praedicatur
notes: Basilica Minor act. Coronation stated: 'anno MDCCCXLIII, auctoritate Petriani Canonicorum Collegii, aureo diademate fuit redimita' (Vatican Chapter, 1843). The act begins on printed p. 324 (rubric and incipit visible in the adjoining passage AAS-55-1963-ocr#323); the coronation sentence itself is on p. 326, which is the passage's printed_page. Incipit taken verbatim from p. 324 ('Mateola' OCR 'Mateola/Mateóla'). Country inferred from the see of Matera, not stated in the act.

rubric_latin: ECCLESIA PRAEPOSITURALIS SANCTI VICTORIS MARTYRIS, IN OPPIDO VULGO «MISSAGLIA» NUNCUPATO, INTRA FINES MEDIOLANENSIS ARCHIDIOECESIS, BASILICAE MINORIS TITULO AC DIGNITATE DECORATUR.
incipit_latin: Piissima eximiaque, intra Archidioeceseos Mediolanensis fines, regio, cui vulgo « Brianza » est nomen, splendida praedita est gemma
notes: Basilica Minor act; the only coronation reference is 'sollemni caerimonia integri saeculi, primi ex quo Cultui patet Praeposituralis Ecclesia, tertii ab Incoronatane [= Incoronatione] Simulacri' — i.e. the August 1947 celebrations mark the third centenary of the crowning of the statue (so c. 1647), but no year and NO papal authority are stated, hence low confidence; a checker should decide whether it belongs in scope. Passage printed_page is 441; the act opens on printed p. 439, used as aas_page. Country inferred from 'Archidioeceseos Mediolanensis'. Church name OCR'd 'Praeposituralis'.

rubric_latin: TITULUS BASILICAE MINORIS CATHEDRALI TEMPLO MONOPOLITANO CONFERTUR
incipit_latin: Inter potiores sacras Apuliae aedes Monopolitanum cathedrale templum iure meritoque accensendum est, ineunte saeculo xii a sancto Romualdo Episcopo
notes: Basilica Minor act stating 'ipsaque Virginis imago anno MDCCLXIX aureo diademate est coronata' (1769); no crowning authority named. The image is painted on wood ('Virginis imago in ligno depicta'). The act also mentions that a Cardinal Legate of Benedict XV attended the 1921 eighth-centenary festivities - not a coronation legation.

rubric_latin: Beata Maria Virgo, vulgo a « Fontenova » appellata, principalis caelestis Patrona dioecesis Pisciensis eligitur.
incipit_latin: Novus veluti fons in huius saeculi desertis spatiis exiit, cum aerumnoso humano generi data est, summo Dei miserentis beneficio, pientissima Mater ac certissimum salutis perfugium, Beata Virgo Maria.
notes: Patronage act attesting the crowning: '... et anno MDCCiixxxn aureo diademate est redimita'. The OCR form 'MDCCiixxxn' resolves to MDCCLXXXII = 1782 on the pattern used elsewhere in this OCR ('MDCCCiiXXXViin' = MDCCCLXXXVIII); a checker should confirm the year against the printed page. No crowning authority named. Act date OCR 'MCMLÍXIII' = MCMLXIII (1963), Pontificatus Nostri primo. Country inferred, not stated.

rubric_latin: Sinitur Archiepiscopus Messanensis nomine atque auctoritate Summi Pontificis imaginem B. M. V. a divina Providentia coronare, quae in urbe Montalbano Elicona, in eadem archidioecesi, colitur.
incipit_latin: Qui singulari semper amore beatissimam Virginem Mariam, Christi Matrem, hominum decus caelique florem, prosecuti sumus et prosequimur
notes: Rubric OCR reads 'B. M. W.'; repaired to 'B. M. V.'. Archbishop: Ignazio Cannavò. Country inferred from the Sicilian place/see (act does not name Italy).

rubric_latin: ECCLESIA BEATAE MARIAE V. IN CAELUM ASSUMPTAE SACRA IN MONTE « CREA » INTRA CASALENSIS DIOECESIS FINES, BASILICAE MINORIS TITULO AC PRIVILEGIIS COHONESTATUR.
incipit_latin: In summo colle « Crea » nuncupato, ex quo omnem Montis Ferrati et Casalensis dioecesis regionem conspicias, nobile exstat templum
notes: Basilica Minor act; coronation attested in passing on printed p. 179: « quae imago die v mensis Augusti, anno MDCCCLXÌXXX, sollemni ritu aurea redimita est corona ». The year is OCR-damaged — raw form 'MDCCCLXÌXXX', read here as MDCCCLXXXX = 1890 (1880 would require two spurious characters); needs human verification. The crowned object is the altarpiece painting of the Assumption by Guglielmo Caccia 'il Moncalvo'. No authorising authority is named.

image_title_vernacular: Madonna di San Martino (B.ma Vergine detta di S. Martino)
citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 188r–204v.[02.mn.0000]
act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, relazione
legate: Abbate Gio. Andrea Ricci (Abbas Joannes Andreas Riccius, Politianus, canon of St Peter's), delegate of the Vatican Chapter
deputy: Abbate Gio. Andrea Ricci (Abbas Joannes Andreas Riccius, Politianus, canon of St Peter's), delegate of the Vatican Chapter
rubric_latin: Relazione del seguito nella Venuta dell'Illmo e Rmo Sig.r Can.co Gio. Andrea Ricci in Montepulciano per coronare la Bma Vergine detta di S. Martino esistente nella Chiesa Cattedrale
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'duas coronas aureas valoris et aestimationis scut. centum monetae Romanae'. f.188r: letter of Gio. Andrea Ricci from Montepulciano, 31 Oct 1707, announcing his arrival and reception by the Bishop, Chapter, Magistrato and the Operai della Madonna di S. Martino. f.189r: silversmith's account ('Adi 30 Sett. 1700' - probably 1707) for two gold crowns, large and small, 153.85 scudi, 'Servirono p le Sacre Immagini della Sma Vergine e Suo Bambino Gesu nella Città di Monte Pulciano'; sums repeated on f.188v; wrapper f.194v 'Conto 2 ... Gio: Giardini Oref.'. ff.190r-192r, 196r-197v and 198r-v: three copies of the 'Relatione del seguito nella venuta ... Can.co Gio. Andrea Ricci in Montepulciano per coronare la Bma Vergine detta di S. Martino esistente nella Chiesa Cattedrale' (arrival dates garbled by OCR: '16 Ott.e 1701', '26 7bre 1760' with margin 'd'an: 1760', '5 Ott.e 1707'; the coronation day 6 November is consistent in all copies and the title leaf f.193v gives 1707). Coronation at the Mass after Communion; an instrument of consignment of the two crowns was rogated by the chancellor of the episcopal curia (not present; f.193v margin '(non vi è l'origine)'). f.195v margin: 'lettera delle M. S. ... Andrea Ricci ...'. The third copy of the relazione breaks off at f.198v, the last page of the range. | Two copies of the relazione (ff. 196r–198v), 'Memorie dello Scoprimento e Culto' drawn from episcopal visitations of 1610/1612 (ff. 200r–200v, two copies; ends 'De Anno 1707 ... ipsa Sacra Imago una cum Imagine Infantis Jesu in ejus sinu sedentis corona aurea fuit solemni pompa coronata'), Ricci's covering letter of the day after the crowning (f. 201r, OCR date 'Montepulciano 7 9.bre 1701' / 'Montegranaro 9 8br 1701', i.e. 7 Nov 1707), a 'Decretum 30 Junii 1704' of which only the heading was transcribed (f. 201v) — taken here as the concession date, medium certainty — and two copies of the notarial instrument of consignment (ff. 202r–203v; notary Oliverius Antonius Vannutius, chancellor Vincentius Pallini/Lattini; authenticated by the vicar general 15/18 Nov 1707; margin: 'Instrum. Donationis ... Politiana die 5. [or 8.] 9bris 1707'). Coronation date: relazione says Ricci arrived 26 Sept (OCR '1760') / 5 Oct 1707 and the ceremony was 'il dì 6. Nov.'; letter 'Coronatione di ieri mattina' confirms 6 Nov 1707; the instrument's OCR 'die sexta Mens. Sept./Feb.' is presumably 'Novembris'. f. 204v margin: 'Altra lettera del d.º S.r Ab.e Ricci ... relat.e ... alla coronaz.ne' (text not transcribed). Isolated margin words 'Antonelli' (f. 199r) and 'loco detto Sevratto' (f. 204v) unexplained — the latter probably belongs to the following Tersatto dossier. f. 196r opens with the head of the relazione; whether earlier Montepulciano documents precede f. 196r cannot be seen from this range. The instrument also alludes to the Chapter having earlier crowned images 'in celeberrimo D. Blasii Templo' (S. Biagio, Montepulciano) — not documented in this range.

image_title_vernacular: Santa Maria di Montevergine (Madonna di Monte Vergine, anticamente detta di Costantinopoli)
citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 215r.[01.mn.0000]–234r
act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, relazione, stampa
legate: Canon Abbot Riccardo Howard of the Dukes of Norfolk (OCR variants: 'Niccardo Sforciade ex Ducibus Novaepholiae', 'Oricordi', 'Ricciardi Abb.', 'Suardo', 'Guardi', 'San-Guardj')
deputy: Canon Abbot Riccardo Howard of the Dukes of Norfolk (OCR variants: 'Niccardo Sforciade ex Ducibus Novaepholiae', 'Oricordi', 'Ricciardi Abb.', 'Suardo', 'Guardi', 'San-Guardj')
register_refs: ['12 Julii 1711 Lib. Decr. XX. fol. 8. t.º', '12. Conv: fol. 93.', 'Arch. Mss. Tom. 12. Canon. fol. 93.', 'Cap. 39. fasc. 329.-', 'V.g. f.315', 'cap. 63. pag: 435.']
rubric_latin: Instrumentum Donationis Duarum Coronæ aureæ, factæ Imagini B. M. V. miraculosæ ... in Sacro, et Reali Monasterio Montis Virginis maioris de Alvito, factæ in Actis Regiis Die 17. Maij 1712
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Three heavily garbled OCR passes of one Latin attestation by the archbishop of Benevento ('Athanasius Ursinus, S. Beneventanae Ecclesiae Archiepiscopus'; signature OCR 'J. d. B. Card. Spinus Archiepiscopus' — i.e. Cardinal Orsini, archbishop of Benevento 1686–1724, inferred), dated Benevento 9 Jan 1708, testifying to the antiquity and miracles of an image of the Virgin painted by St Luke: brought by Baldwin, Emperor of Constantinople; 'Catharina Balduini'; Frederick's army 'anno 1239 juxta Beneventanam'; 'Brundusium'; 'Civitate Abellina' (Avellino); 'Monte praefato adscendere'; 'Guilelmo Abbati'; 'Congregationis Montis Virginis' — legend elements pointing to the Madonna di Montevergine, but one pass places the image 'in Ecclesia S. Angeli ...' (S. Angelo a Cupolo?) and another 'Monialium Asceterii', so the church is not securely read. Margin 'Car. ly / januarij Co:nat.' (Coronat.?) and '2/3'. Attestation only: no decree, crowns, deputy or coronation date in this range; dossier presumably continues past f. 215r. Wrapper f. 214v 'Corone d'oro' (margin '514') may belong to this dossier. | Dossier contents: (a) attestations on the origin of the image by the Archbishop of Benevento (OCR 'Athanasius Ursinus' / 'Card. Spinus Archiepiscopus', i.e. Card. Orsini), dated 9 January 1708, margin 'Attestati circa l'origine della Madonna di Monte Vergine nella Diocesi di Benevento, o sia Provincia del 1708' and 'Monte Vergine a del 1708' (heavily garbled Latin, ff. 215r–218v); (b) conto of the silversmith Gio. Giardini for two crowns 'per mandare alla Chiesa detta di Monte uergine di Napoli', settled 23 May 1711, 295 scudi (ff. 216r–217v); (c) decree 12 July 1711 (Lib. Decr. XX f. 8v) suspending the coronation because the image already had a gold crown, remitting the question to the Nuncio (f. 219r); (d) notarial copy of the donation instrument by D. Thomas Cervanetta of Mercogliano, dated in the text 'Die Decimoquarto mensis Maij' 1712 (margin says 17 May 1712), incorporating the Chapter's commission letter of Rome 24 [April] 1712, the 'Ordo servandi in Tradendis Coronis Aureis', and the brief of Clement XI of 29 April 1712 granting a plenary indulgence (ff. 220r–223v); (e) relazione of Canon Howard's journey (25 April–21 May 1712), coronation performed after first Vespers of Pentecost, i.e. Saturday 14 May 1712 (heading 'alli 14. di Maggio 1712'), ff. 224r–229v, with a printed 'avviso' from Naples quoted; (f) letter of the Abbot General D. Vito Antonio Pastorale, Montevergine 15 May 1712, and minuta of the Chapter's reply 5 June (or Aug.) 1712 (ff. 230v–233v). No explicit concession date appears; the Chapter's letter says only 'havendo Noi già da molto tempo Decretata la Corona d'oro'. Margin at f. 223v reads 'Montis Virginis maioris de Alvito' (OCR; expected 'de Monte'). 'cap. 63. pag: 435.' (f. 229r) and 'Lib. III. de S. M. V. a pag. 25' (f. 230r) may be bibliographic rather than register references.

legate: Cardinalis Ruffo Scilla
rubric_latin: NEAPOLITANA. DECRETUM INTRODUCTIONIS CAUSAE PRO BEATIFICATIONE ET CANONIZATIONE VENERABILIS SERVI DEI PLACIDI BACCHER, PRESBYTERI SAECULARIS E TERTIO ORDINE S. DOMINICI, RECTORIS VETERIS ECCLESIAE SS. NOMINI IESU DICATAE IN URBE NEAPOLITANA.
incipit_latin: Dives in misericordia Deus congruentem temporibus conferens opem, in sinu Ecclesiae suae opportune suscitat sacerdotes, Christi spiritu plenos
notes: Crowning attested in passing in the biographical section of the decree: 'auctoritate et decreto Rmi Capituli vaticani, die xxx Decembris a. MDCCCXXVI, ab eiusdem Capituli delegato, Cardinali Ruffo Scilla, aurea corona decoratum fuit'. Ruffo Scilla acted as delegate of the Vatican Chapter, not as papal Legate. The decree begins on printed p. 498 (passage printed_page is 500, where the coronation is mentioned). act_date is the Congregation's session date (die iv Maii MDCCCCIX); Pius X signed the commission on 12 May 1909.

rubric_latin: NEAPOLITANA. BEATIFICATIONIS ET CANONIZATIONIS VENERABILIS SERVI DEI PLACIDI BACCHER, SACERDOTIS SAECULARIS E TERTIO ORDINE S. DOMINICI. SUPER DUBIO
incipit_latin: In Neapolitana civitate, fecunda Servorum Dei altrice, e nobili prosapia, ortus est Placidus Baccher die 5 Aprilis a. 1781 eodemque die baptizatus est
notes: Decree on the heroic virtues of Ven. Placido Baccher; coronation mentioned only in passing: '...atque erga Beatissimam Virginem, cuius immaculati conceptus doctrinam, ante dogmaticam definitionem, strenue defendit, cuius etiam simulacrum in sua Ecclesia veneratum, a Vaticano Capitulo corona decorandum curavit'. No date; the image is the one venerated in the church 'Gesù Vecchio' in Naples of which Baccher was rector. Passage printed_page 153; decree opens on p. 152.

rubric_latin: BASILICAE MINORIS HONORIBUS PRIVILEGIISQUE AFFICITUR ECCLESIA, QUAE VULGO « GESÙ VECCHIO » APPELLATUR, NEAPOLI EXSTANS.
incipit_latin: Parthenopen urbem praeclaram augusta Virgo, singulari ducta studio amoris, elegisse videtur, ubi non solum unum, sed plura constitueret domicilia pietatis
notes: « Iuvat quoque memorare id anno MDCCCXXVI, auctoritate Vaticani Canonicorum Collegii, aurea corona esse redimitum » — crowned 1826 by authority of the Vatican Chapter. The act adds that Pius IX celebrated before the image at Naples on 9 Sept 1849. Statue set up for public veneration by Ven. Placido Baccher. aas_page = 34, where the act begins (batch passage paginated 35). This act also appears at the end of passage AAS-51-1959-ocr#33.

rubric_latin: " PARVUM SANCTUARIUM MARIAE VIRGINIS PERDOLENTIS VULGO ' AL FIUMICELLO ' ", QUOD NEAPOLI EXSTAT, PONTIFICIO COGNOMINE PERPETUO DECORATUR.
incipit_latin: Romani Pontifices Decessores Nostri, ut Christiani populi religio ac pietas erga Deiparam Virginem magis magisque augescerent in dies
notes: Pius X granted the Archbishop of Naples the faculty to crown the image ('facultatem libenter fecit, ut simulacrum eiusdem B. Virginis ... aurea corona redimiret'); it was carried out in the metropolitan church on 4 September 1910 in the Pope's name and by his authority by the Cardinal Archbishop, who is not named in the text. The act is dated 1916 although printed in AAS vol. 9 (1917); this is confirmed by the surrounding acts, which run in date order from Oct. 1914 to Feb. 1916, and by 'Pontificatus Nostri anno secundo'.

rubric_latin: TEMPLUM VULGO «DEL CARMINE MAGGIORE» NUNCUPATUM CIVITATIS NEAPOLITANAE IN BASILICAM MINOREM ERIGITUR.

notes: Basilica minor act; coronation stated in passing: « Novissime prodigiosa Imago anno millesimo octingentesimo septuagesimo quinto a Capitulo Nostro Vaticano diademate aureo sollemni pompa redimita fuit ». Crowned by the Vatican Chapter, not personally by the Pope. The act opens on printed page 12 (rubric + 'Ad perpetuam rei memoriam'); the coronation clause falls on page 13, so aas_page is the act's START page.

rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA V., « DE PONTE » APPELLATA, PATRONA CAELESTIS AEQUE PRINCIPALIS CUM S. IUVENALE CIVITATIS AC DIOECESIS NARNIENSIS DECLARATUR.
incipit_latin: Viam vitae insistentes Christifideles tot inter pericula et acerbitates, recto haud labuntur itinere et ad locum petitum, sempiternam dicimus beatitatem, feliciter perveniunt
notes: Patron declaration; attests 'Simulacrum Almae Deiparae de Ponte ... a Carolo Maria Cardinali Sacripante, anno millesimo septingentesimo quinquagesimo quarto, auctoritate Petriani Canonicorum Collegii, est aureo diademate inter acclamantis populi vota redimitum' — crowned in 1754 by Cardinal Carlo Maria Sacripante on the authority of the Vatican Chapter. A commemorative liturgical feast on 5 May was afterwards instituted with the approval of Pius IX. The image (BVM holding the Divine Child) was found in 1714. Vernacular form 'Madonna del Ponte' rendered from the Latin 'de Ponte'. Act begins on printed page 758 (passage indexed at 759).

legate: Iosephus S. R. E. Cardinalis Casoria, Praefectus Sacrae Congregationis pro Sacramentis et Cultu Divino

Petition of Bp Iolandus Nuzzi, letter of 16 April 1983; tercentenary celebrations that year; image given to the Carmelite nuns in the 17th century at the request of Ven. Seraphina a Deo. Country inferred from the Italian title and the see of Nocera; not named in the act.

rubric_latin: Beata Maria Virgo, « Scala Paradisi » appellata, principalis Patrona, et S. Conradus Confalonieri, Confessor, Patronus aeque principalis totius Netensis dioecesis constituuntur.
incipit_latin: Scandere caelum datur hominibus, qui Beatae Mariae Virgini se devovent eiusque ductu vitam degunt cum virtute.
notes: Patronage act attesting the crowning: 'imago illa, auctoritate Petriani Collegii Canonicorum, anno MCMXXXI, aureo diademate fuit redimita' (Vatican Chapter, 1931). Act date OCR 'MCMUXIII' = MCMLXIII. Country inferred, not stated. Vernacular form of the title supplied from the Latin epithet - verify.

incipit_latin: Templa Dei, quae, magno pietatis studio circumfusa, amplitudinis non minus quam artis operibus ditata, singulari Christifidelium frequentia celebrantur

M. V. de Oropa'. The year and authority of the crowning itself are not stated - needs human check. Country Italy inferred from 'in Pedemontana regione'; act begins on printed page 951.

rubric_latin: dat, donat, et concedit Be- atissimæ Virgini nuncupat. S.ti Brijj huius Ill.mo Civitatis Urbevetanae ... Duas Coronas Aureas ... in antiquiss. et Insigni Ecclesia Cathedrali
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'Duas Coronas Aureas', weight 7½ oz and 2 denari of gold, 276 scudi 8 [baiocchi?] Roman money excluding the goldsmith's fee. Petitioner: City of Orvieto (Confaloniere e Conservatori / publico Consiglio) through Bishop Vincenzo de' Conti degli Atti; crowns received in the instrument by Giovanni Battista Gualterio, camerlengo of the Fabbrica of the Cathedral. Only the first two pages of the Latin donation instrument fall within this range (f.142r–v); it breaks off at 'coronata' and continues past the range. Coronation date is the date of the instrument (8 June 1704, Clement XI anno IV), which states the crowns were brought 'ad effectum coronandi' and that the images were 'postea coram eisdem ... coronata' — read as same-day crowning, not explicitly confirmed. Diocese inferred from 'Civitatis Urbevetanae' and the mention of its bishop. The deputy's surname is OCR-garbled ('Cia- Siy Coccianus'); the bishop is named only as 'R.mo D. Fabritio Ep.'. No concession decree or margin note is visible in this range. The image is apparently the Madonna venerated in the Cappella di S. Brizio of Orvieto Cathedral (the text says 'nuncupat. S.ti Brijj'); the Child is named ('illiusque D.ni Filij'). The margin note on f.122r mentioning an 'Ab.te d'Orvieto: Andrea Ricci' may relate to this dossier. | Instrument of donation dated 8 June 1704 (notary Carlo Fontana of Orvieto), witnesses Leone Albergio and Monaldo Aurelio; the printed Racconto (by canon Lattanzio Silvestrucci, Orvieto: Livio Tosini) confirms the crowning on 8 June 1704 during solemn Mass, with feasts 8-10 June; a sonnet to D. Annibale Albani at f.159v. Margin note at f.143v reads 'conceditur 16 Jul. 1896' — year clearly garbled by OCR (1696 or 1703 possible), so concession_date left null; the same note reads 'Instrum. donationis duarum Coronarum aurearum factae Imaginis miraculosae B. M. V. in Ecclesia ... Civitatis Urbevet. ... die 27. May 1704' (partly garbled). The image was formerly called 'Santa Maria prisca' and 'S. Maria della Stella'. The bishop's name is garbled as 'Fabritio Ep.' in the Latin instrument but given as Vincenzo de' Conti degli Atti in the Racconto.

notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), value 78 1/2 scudi d'oro in oro. Petitioner: Clero e Città d'Otranto; concession originally granted at the prayers of Card. de Aste (then a member of the Chapter). Concession date taken from the endorsement on f.82r ('Instrum Donationis duar Coronar aurear / concessio 14 Maii 1691', with silversmith Gio. Giardini's signature on f.82v); its attribution to Otranto is inferred (medium) from the 1705 letter stating the crown had been 'destinata' earlier at Card. de Aste's request and from the archbishop's information letter of 6/20 June 1691 (two copies, ff.83r-84r, endorsed 'Lettera di Mons. Arcivescovo d'Otranto in ordine alla Corona d'oro'). Instrument (two copies, ff.87r-88r) is dated 'Die vero Septima Martij' 1705, notary Angelo Stephanoch of Otranto; the archivist's endorsement reads '7 Maij 1705' but the archbishop's covering letter of 22 March 1705 (f.89r) confirms March. Conto on f.85r (Dom.co Vannini) for two crowns, 154:50 in all, sits inside this dossier and is presumed to belong to it. The 1691 letter records the statue's return from Valona (Vlorë) after the Turkish sack of 1480 and a jubilee granted by Pius V in 1564. Loose margin words 'Oronzo', '14', '85' on ff.85v-86v.

Legate named in the text only by praenomen and office ('dilecto Filio Nostro Aristidi Cardinali Patriarchae Venetiarum' = Aristide Cavallari); surname not in the text, so not supplied. Coronation to take place 'mense maio vertente' 1909, hence year only. Country inferred from Padua/Venice, hence medium.

legate: S. R. E. Cardinalis Cavallari, Venetiarum Patriarcha

The ceremony date is not given. Margin numbers 179-183 are the booklet's pagination; f.185v margin '31-90 33-70 40 65' are sums.

Romæ 7 9mbris 1704' while the Chapter's Italian letter (f. 108r) is dated 'Roma 4. 9mbre 1707' (addressed 'Monsignor Corelli Vescovo di M.feltro', OCR for Martorelli) - year uncertain. The instrument's church reading 'Eccl.ia S.ti Arch.li Mich.is' conflicts with S. Christophori elsewhere and is probably OCR. Margin label f. 110v gives 'die 15. Aug.ti 1709' and the bishop's attestation 'Die 21 Augusti 1705' - both likely OCR/slips for 1708. The confraternity (Società della B. V. delle Grazie; deputies Gio. Carboni, Polidoro Valentini, Giuseppe Fabri) received the crowns and undertook the obligation. The cover f. 111v ('Decernitur Visitatio 10 Maii 1694 conceditur 11 Oct 1694') immediately follows this dossier but appears to belong to the unidentified 'Conto 2' at f. 112r; it may nevertheless be this image's concession.

rubric_latin: TEMPLUM B. MARIAE V., PLACENTINA IN URBE, « SANTA MARIA DI CAMPAGNA » APPELLATUM, BASILICAE MINORIS TITULO AC PRIVILEGIIS COHONESTATUR.
incipit_latin: Placentia, urbs ampla, non uno commendatur Templo artificiosis operibus nobili populique concursibus celebrato
notes: Basilica Minor elevation; attests the image was crowned 'anno millesimo sexcentesimo secundo, iterumque hoc vertente anno, aureo diademate a Purpurato Ecclesiae Patre Francisco Borgongini-Duca, quem nuper defunctum deflevimus, Nostro nomine et auctoritate'. Two crownings: 1602 (authority not specified) and a re-crowning in the current year, i.e. 1954, by Card. Borgongini-Duca in the Pope's name (he died 4 Aug 1954, so before that date). Act dated 3 Nov 1954 (Datum line taken from the full volume text, beyond the passage excerpt; confirmed by the volume index). Diocese name 'Placentina' supplied from 'Placentina in urbe'/'Piacentini Archiepiscopi-Episcopi Adiutor'; country Italy inferred - hence medium confidence.

notes: Basilica Minor act; coronation attested only in passing and without authority or date: 'sacram illam Beatissimae Virginis effigiem, pretioso diademate iterum iterumque cinctam, egregium iam a saeculo xvi templum contegit' - the image has been crowned more than once. Act date from 'die duo de tricesimo mensis Novembris' = 28 November 1971. Country inferred from Rhegium/Reggio Calabria. OCR prints 'nobilitai' for 'nobilitat' (repaired).

rubric_latin: AD R. P. D. VINCENTIUM SCOZZOLI, ARIMINENSIUM EPISCOPUM, SAECULO IAM EXEUNTE, EX QUO S. P. PIUS VII, V. R., E GALLICA CAPTIVITATE REDUX, SIMULACRUM SSMAE VIRGINIS MARIAE, ARIMINENSIBUS SACRUM, DIADEMATE EXORNAVIT.
incipit_latin: Pervetustum istud Virginis augustae simulacrum, non tradita tantum a maioribus religione scimus esse Ariminensibus sacerrimum
notes: Pius VII crowned the image in person while passing through Rimini on his return from captivity in France: 'qui Ariminum pertransiens e gallica redux captivitate ... regio illud diademate ornavit'. No year is given; the 1914 letter says the century is drawing to a close ('saeculo iam exeunte'), which implies c. 1814 - not stated, so coronation_date left null. Datum reads 'die viri aprilis' in the OCR = die VIII aprilis. The same act is indexed at AAS 6 (1914) 733 and 762.

legate: Clemens S. R. E. Cardinalis Micara, Bishop of Velletri, Pro-Prefect of the Sacred Congregation of Rites
rubric_latin: BEATAE MARIAE V. VULGO « DEI LÀTTANI » DICTA, TITULO « REGINA MUNDI » HONESTATA, DIOECESIUM CALVENSIS ET THEANENSIS CAELESTIS PATRONA CONFIRMATUR.
incipit_latin: Vitae huius iactati procellis atque tenebris offusi, Christifideles oportet ad Almam Deiparam fidentibus animis confugiant, quae, ex providentis Dei consilio
notes: Patron-declaration act; coronation attested in passing on printed p. 149: « postquam die vi mensis Augusti, anno MCML, per Venerabilem Fratrem Nostrum Clementem Sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae Cardinalem Micara ... Imago illa, inter populi gestientis vota, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, aurea redimita est corona ». The act names no town, only the two dioceses, so locality is left null. Country inferred from the Italian dioceses of Calvi and Teano.

rubric_latin: Templum Beatae Mariae Virginis Reginae mundi in civitate Arcismonfina, in dioecesi Calvensi et Theanensi, titulo Basilicae Minoris decoratur.
incipit_latin: Quanto studio quantoque amore christianae aetates fuerint erga sanctissimam Christi Matrem, auxilium atque praesidium tutissimum populi christiani, id luculentissime ostendunt tum templa augusta ubique gentium structa
notes: Basilica Minor act. The only coronation evidence is descriptive: 'atque imaginem sanctam e petra beatissimae Matris, aurea redimita corona, quae ibi est, turbae frequentissimae petunt' - a stone image already wearing a golden crown; no crowning authority, decree or date is stated, so papal authorship of the coronation is NOT established by this passage. 'civitas Arcismonfina' read as Roccamonfina (Caserta) - verify; country inferred from the diocese of Calvi e Teano. aas_page set to 204, where the rubric and act begin (the crowned-image sentence falls on p. 205, the indexed printed_page).

rubric_latin: AD REVMUM P. MC CABE PATRITIUM, MISSIONALIUM A SS. CORDE IESU SUPREMUM MODERATOREM, OB VERTENS SAECULUM AB EADEM CONGREGATIONE CONDITA.
incipit_latin: Cum percepimus te sodalesque tuos in eo esse, ut fauste primum explendum saeculum, ex quo religiosum Institutum Missionalium a SS. Corde Iesu conditum fuit, celebraretis
notes: Clause: « ex augusto religionis ritu, quo in urbana aede sacra Deiparae Dominae a SS. Corde Iesu eiusdem iconi aureum imposituri estis sertum » — an imminent, not yet performed, crowning. « Urbana aedes » is taken as the Roman church of the Missionaries of the Sacred Heart (the letter says « cum Romae vos festum coetum agetis »); the church is not named outright, hence confidence medium. No papal grant of the coronation is stated in this letter.

rubric_latin: URBIS. Templum Ss.mi Cordis Iesu ad Castrum Praetorium diaconia fit
incipit_latin: Almae Urbis templa, quae vel antiquitate excellerent artisque praestantia vel illustrium sanctorumque virorum memoria, consueverunt Romani Pontifices singularibus privilegiis atque honoribus afficere.
notes: Apostolic Constitution erecting the church as a cardinalitial deaconry; it attests in passing: 'in eaque, exstans ibique venerata effigies Beatae Mariae Virginis Auxiliatricis rite a Canonicis patriarchalis Basilicae S. Petri aurea corona redimita est' (crowned by the canons of the Vatican Basilica), with no date given. Act begins on printed p. 485; the coronation sentence runs onto p. 486 (the passage's printed_page). Vernacular title supplied from the Latin.

deputy: Michele Angelo Mattei and Camillo Mugiara, canons of the Basilica, delivered the crowns (f. 99r); account approved by 'Palmieri d'Annunzia Can. Decano Deputato' (f. 98v, name garbled)

notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Margin f. 100v: 'conceditur 28 9bris 1693' and 'consignatio ... Lib. XIX. f.º 387'. Giardini's account (f. 98r-98v) for two crowns for 'la SS.ma Madonna e Suo Bambino di S. Pantaleo in Roma', total 166:95, 100 scudi on account 19 Dec 1693. The coronation_date is the date of the Latin receipt (f. 99r, 'Die 25. Martij 1694') in which the Piarist Praepositus Generalis Jo. Franciscus a S. The 'Breve relazione dell'origine' (f. 101r-101v) gives the image's history (painted by an anonymous Perugian painter, given by Aurora Berti to the Piarists); 'Insignificanz.a' in the margin is OCR.

notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Silversmith's account only (total 266:95, 200 received on account via the Baldeschi, balance 66:95; 'A 19 Xmbre 1693' payment of 100 scudi on account). Dated 1693 by the payment entry. Last leaf of the range; the dossier presumably continues on f.99r.

rubric_latin: ECCLESIA SANCTAE MARIAE ANGELORUM IN URBE AD BASILICAM MINOREM EVEHITUR.
incipit_latin: Titulum sancti Cyriaci in Thermis, fidei christianorum tempore Diocletiani imperatoris perinsigne monumentum, inde ab anno 1091 Carthusianis commissum
notes: Basilica Minor act; states 'Quod quidem simulacrum die 27 elapsi mensis iunii, hoc anno, aureo diademate Ordo Canonicorum sacrosanctae Nostrae Basilicae Vaticanae pro instituto suo sollemniter decoravit' - crowned by the Vatican Chapter on 27 June 1920. Act begins on printed page 435 (passage printed_page is 436). The image was set up for public veneration by the priest Antonio Del Duca.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 102r–103v
rubric_latin: Serve la d.ta Corona per la S.ma Madonna Delli Sette Dolori Esistente Nella Chiesa delli R. R. P.P. Serviti di S. Marcello
notes: Crowns: one (large crown for the Virgin). Only Giardini's account survives here: a single large gold crown with foliage, cherub heads, arms and engraved letters, 74:2 scudi of gold, total 144:25, 60 scudi received 11 Jan 1695; appraised by Orsino Reposati. Cover f. 103v margin: 'Decreta 16 aug. 1694 consignatio ... Lib. XIX f. 540'; the margin 'n. 1694 . 540.' at the head of f. 104r probably repeats this reference. No relazione or instrument in range.

citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 186r–187v
rubric_latin: doi corone d'oro una p la S.mma Madon.a e l'altra p il suo S.mo Bambino detta la Madona del Nome di Maria assistente nella Chiesa di S. Bernardo alla Colonna Traiana
notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Only a silversmith's account (undated, total 177.99 scudi; margin 'B 9') on f.186r, with its wrapper label on f.187v 'Dell R.mo Capitolo di S. Pietro della Corona d'oro - Con Gio Giardini Arfe.º' carrying the margin note 'Decr. 19 aug. 1703 Donat. coronat. abina u. L. XXI. f.º 318.' The concession date and register reference are taken from that wrapper note on the assumption that ff.186-187 form one bifolium; the same note could conceivably belong to the following Montepulciano dossier (crowned 1707). 'abina u.' is garbled (perhaps 'ibidem').
